160.12.span: Coverage for the use of NMES/FES is limited to SCI patients for walking, who have completed a training program which consists of at least 32 physical therapy sessions with the device over a period of three months.

160.12.text: FES training directly performed by the physical therapist, one-on-one
160.12.span: Physical therapy necessary to perform this training must be directly performed by the physical therapist as part of a one-on-one training program.

160.12.text: FES: intact lower motor units (L1 and below)
160.12.span: Persons with intact lower motor units (L1 and below) (both muscle and peripheral nerve);

160.12.text: FES: independent transfers and independent standing tolerance >= 3 minutes
160.12.span: Persons that can transfer independently and can demonstrate independent standing tolerance for at least 3 minutes;

160.12.text: FES: at least 6 months post recovery from SCI and restorative surgery
160.12.span: Persons with at least 6-month post recovery spinal cord injury and restorative surgery;

160.12.text: FES: brisk muscle contraction to NMES and sufficient sensory perception
160.12.span: Persons that demonstrate brisk muscle contraction to NMES and have sensory perception electrical stimulation sufficient for muscle contraction;

160.12.text: FES: goal is walking, not reversing muscle atrophy
160.12.span: The goal of physical therapy must be to train SCI patients on the use of NMES/FES devices to achieve walking, not to reverse or retard muscle atrophy.

160.18.text: Epilepsy: medically refractory partial onset seizures and surgery not recommended or failed
160.18.span: VNS is reasonable and necessary for patients with medically refractory partial onset seizures for whom surgery is not recommended or for whom surgery has failed

160.18.text: All other seizure types are non-covered
160.18.span: VNS is not reasonable and necessary for all other types of seizure disorders which are medically refractory and for whom surgery is not recommended or for whom surgery has failed

160.18.text: TRD covered only within a CMS-approved CED study
160.18.span: VNS is non-covered for the treatment of TRD when furnished outside of a CMS-approved CED study.

160.18.text: TRD: current MDD episode >= 2 years or >= 4 MDD episodes including current
160.18.span: The patient must be in a major depressive disorder (MDD) episode for ≥ two years or have had at least four episodes of MDD, including the current episode.

160.18.text: TRD: at least four prior failed treatments of adequate dose and duration, measured by a tool
160.18.span: The patient’s depressive illness meets a minimum criterion of four prior failed treatments of adequate dose and duration as measured by a tool designed for this purpose.

160.18.text: TRD: MDE measured by a guideline-recommended scale on two visits within 45 days before implant
160.18.span: The patient is experiencing a major depressive episode (MDE) as measured by a guideline recommended depression scale assessment tool on two visits, within a 45-day span prior to implantation of the VNS device.

160.18.text: TRD: stable medication regimen for at least four weeks before implant
160.18.span: Patients must maintain a stable medication regimen for at least four weeks before device implantation.

160.18.text: TRD exclusion: current or lifetime psychotic features in any MDE
160.18.span: Current or lifetime history of psychotic features in any MDE

160.18.text: Replacement for TRD patients at battery end of life or device malfunction
160.18.span: Patients implanted with a VNS device for TRD may receive a VNS device replacement if it is required due to the end of battery life, or any other device-related malfunction.

160.24.text: FDA-approved DBS device (or Category B IDE trial protocol)
160.24.span: Medicare will only consider DBS devices to be reasonable and necessary if they are Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved devices for DBS

160.24.text: VIM: ET (postural/kinetic hand tremor without other neurologic signs) or tremor-dominant idiopathic PD
160.24.span: Diagnosis of ET based on postural or kinetic tremors of hand(s) without other neurologic signs, or diagnosis of idiopathic PD (presence of at least 2 cardinal PD features (tremor, rigidity or bradykinesia)) which is of a tremor-dominant form

160.24.text: VIM: disabling tremor at least level 3 or 4 on Fahn-Tolosa-Marin despite optimal medical therapy
160.24.span: Marked disabling tremor of at least level 3 or 4 on the Fahn-Tolosa-Marin Clinical Tremor Rating Scale (or equivalent scale) in the extremity intended for treatment, causing significant limitation in daily activities despite optimal medical therapy

160.24.text: Willing and able to cooperate during awake surgery and post-op adjustments
160.24.span: Willingness and ability to cooperate during conscious operative procedure, as well as during post-surgical evaluations, adjustments of medications and stimulator settings

160.24.text: STN/GPi: advanced idiopathic PD by Hoehn and Yahr or UPDRS III
160.24.span: Advanced idiopathic PD as determined by the use of Hoehn and Yahr stage or Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) part III motor subscale

160.24.text: STN/GPi: L-dopa responsive with clearly defined on periods
160.24.span: L-dopa responsive with clearly defined "on" periods

160.24.text: STN/GPi: persistent disabling symptoms or drug side effects despite optimal medical therapy
160.24.span: Persistent disabling Parkinson's symptoms or drug side effects (e.g., dyskinesias, motor fluctuations, or disabling "off" periods) despite optimal medical therapy

160.24.text: Exclusion: non-idiopathic PD or Parkinson-plus syndromes
160.24.span: Non-idiopathic Parkinson's disease or "Parkinson's Plus" syndromes

160.24.text: Exclusion: cognitive impairment, dementia or depression that would worsen or interfere
160.24.span: Cognitive impairment, dementia or depression, which would be worsened by or would interfere with the patient's ability to benefit from DBS

160.24.text: Exclusion: current psychosis, alcohol or drug abuse
160.24.span: Current psychosis, alcohol abuse or other drug abuse

160.24.text: Exclusion: previous movement disorder surgery in the affected basal ganglion
160.24.span: Previous movement disorder surgery within the affected basal ganglion

160.24.text: Movement disorders specialist involved in patient selection and post-procedure care
160.24.span: Physicians specializing in movement disorders must be involved in both patient selection and post-procedure care

160.24.text: Exclusion: structural lesion (basal ganglionic stroke, tumor, vascular malformation) as etiology of the movement disorder
160.24.span: Structural lesions such as basal ganglionic stroke, tumor or vascular malformation as etiology of the movement disorder

160.24.text: STN/GPi: diagnosis of PD with at least 2 cardinal features
160.24.span: Diagnosis of PD based on the presence of at least 2 cardinal PD features (tremor, rigidity or bradykinesia)

160.24.text: Exclusion: significant co-morbidities contraindicating DBS surgery or stimulation
160.24.span: Significant medical, surgical, neurologic or orthopedic co-morbidities contraindicating DBS surgery or stimulation

190.14.text: Strong clinical suspicion supported by one or more listed clinical findings
190.14.span: Diagnostic testing to establish HIV infection may be indicated when there is a strong clinical suspicion supported by one or more of the following clinical findings

190.14.text: Western blot only after documentation that initial EIA tests are repeatedly positive or equivocal on a single sample
190.14.span: The Western Blot test should be performed only after documentation that the initial EIA tests are repeatedly positive or equivocal on a single sample.

190.14.text: HIV antigen tests have no defined diagnostic usage
190.14.span: The HIV antigen tests currently have no defined diagnostic usage.

190.14.text: Viral RNA when serology does not establish the diagnosis but strong suspicion persists
190.14.span: Direct viral RNA detection may be performed in those situations where serologic testing does not establish a diagnosis but strong clinical suspicion persists

190.14.text: No repeat testing once initial serology confirms HIV infection
190.14.span: If initial serologic tests confirm an HIV infection, repeat testing is not indicated.

190.14.text: After a negative EIA with no indication for RNA testing, retest interval is 3-6 months
190.14.span: If initial serologic tests are HIV EIA negative and there is no indication for confirmation of infection by viral RNA detection, the interval prior to retesting is 3-6 months.

190.14.text: Indication: blood/body-fluid exposure with antiviral therapy initiated or anticipated
190.14.span: The patient has documented exposure to blood or body fluids known to be capable of transmitting HIV (for example, needle sticks and other significant blood exposures) and antiviral therapy is initiated or anticipated to be initiated.

190.14.text: Indication: documented, otherwise unexplained AIDS-defining or AIDS-associated opportunistic infection
190.14.span: The patient has a documented, otherwise unexplained, AIDS-defining or AIDS-associated opportunistic infection.

190.14.text: Indication: signs and symptoms of acute retroviral syndrome
190.14.span: The patient has signs and symptoms of acute retroviral syndrome with fever, malaise, lymphadenopathy, and skin rash.

200.3.text: Clinical diagnosis of MCI due to AD or mild AD dementia
200.3.span: for patients who have a clinical diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD or mild AD dementia
both with confirmed presence of amyloid beta pathology consistent with AD

200.3.text: Traditional-approval drugs: only in CMS-approved prospective comparative studies (registry allowed)
200.3.span: Monoclonal antibodies directed against amyloid that are approved by the FDA for the treatment of AD based upon evidence of efficacy from a direct measure of clinical benefit may be covered in CMS-approved prospective comparative studies

200.3.text: Accelerated-approval (surrogate endpoint) drugs: only in an RCT under an IND
200.3.span: based upon evidence of efficacy from a change in a surrogate endpoint (e.g., amyloid reduction) considered as reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit may be covered in a randomized controlled trial conducted under an investigational new drug (IND) application

Monoclonal antibodies directed against amyloid indicated for the treatment of AD are covered when furnished according to the FDA approved indication in National Institutes of Health (NIH)-supported trials

200.3.text: Non-covered outside FDA RCTs, CMS-approved studies, or NIH-supported studies
200.3.span: provided outside of an FDAapproved randomized controlled trial, CMS-approved studies, or studies supported by the NIH, are nationally non-covered

210.2.text: Ordered by a physician or authorized practitioner
210.2.span: are covered under Medicare Part B when ordered by a physician (or authorized practitioner) under one of the following conditions

210.2.text: No such test in the preceding two years, or a woman of childbearing age as described in §1861(nn)
210.2.span: She has not had such a test during the preceding two years or is a woman of childbearing age

210.2.text: More frequent testing: evidence of high risk from history/findings AND practitioner recommends testing more often than every two years
210.2.span: There is evidence (on the basis of her medical history or other findings) that she is at high risk of developing cervical cancer and her physician (or authorized practitioner) recommends that she have the test performed more frequently than every two years.

210.2.text: High-risk factor: early onset of sexual activity (under 16)
210.2.span: Early onset of sexual activity (under 16 years of age)

210.2.text: High-risk factor: five or more lifetime sexual partners
210.2.span: Multiple sexual partners (five or more in a lifetime)

210.2.text: §1861(nn) woman: childbearing age with an abnormal Pap in any of the preceding 3 years, or high risk
210.2.span: A woman as described in §1861(nn) of the Act is a woman who is of childbearing age and has had a pap smear test during any of the preceding 3 years that indicated the presence of cervical or vaginal cancer or other abnormality, or is at high risk of developing cervical or vaginal cancer.

210.2.text: Childbearing age: premenopausal and so determined by a physician or qualified practitioner
210.2.span: A woman of childbearing age is one who is premenopausal and has been determined by a physician or other qualified practitioner to be of childbearing age, based upon the medical history or other findings.

210.2.text: Screening pelvic exam should include at least 7 of 11 listed elements
210.2.span: A screening pelvic examination (including a clinical breast examination) should include at least seven of the following eleven elements

210.3.text: FOBT: one per 12 months, i.e., at least 11 months after the month of the last covered screening FOBT
210.3.span: Medicare will cover one gFOBT or one iFOBT at a frequency of every 12 months; i.e., at least 11 months have passed following the month in which the last covered screening FOBT was performed
The minimum age for FOBT is reduced to 45 years and older.

210.3.text: FOBT: written order from the attending physician/PA/NP/CNS
210.3.span: This screening requires a written order from the beneficiary's attending physician
Non-Invasive Biomarker tests are covered once every 3 years

210.3.text: Biomarker: ordered by physician/PA/NP/CNS who will use results in management
210.3.span: When ordered by the physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or clinical nurse specialist who will use the results in the management of the patient.

210.3.text: Biomarker: asymptomatic (no lower GI pain, blood in stool, positive biomarker test, etc.)
210.3.span: Asymptomatic (no signs or symptoms of colorectal disease including but not limited to lower gastrointestinal pain, blood in stool, positive non-invasive biomarker colorectal cancer screening test)

210.3.text: Biomarker: average risk (no personal history of adenomatous polyps, CRC, IBD; no family history of CRC, adenomatous polyps, FAP, HNPCC)
210.3.span: At average risk of developing colorectal cancer (no personal history of adenomatous polyps, colorectal cancer, or inflammatory bowel disease, including Crohn's Disease and ulcerative colitis; no family history of colorectal cancers or adenomatous polyps, familial adenomatous polyposis, or hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer)

210.3.text: Biomarker: patient given information on test performance and need for follow-on colonoscopy if positive
210.3.span: Provided with information about the test performance and the importance of a follow-on colonoscopy if the test returns a positive result.

210.3.text: Biomarker: FDA market authorized and indicated for CRC screening
210.3.span: The test must be Food and Drug Administration (FDA) market authorized and indicated for colorectal cancer screening

210.3.text: Biomarker: processed in a CLIA-certified laboratory
210.3.span: The test must be processed in a CLIA certified laboratory

210.3.text: Biomarker: sensitivity >= 90% and specificity >= 87%, OR sensitivity >= 79% and specificity >= 90%
210.3.span: a sensitivity of greater than or equal to 90% and a specificity greater than or equal to 87%, OR Criteria 2, a sensitivity of greater than or equal to 79% and a specificity of greater than or equal to 90%

210.3.text: All other CRC screening indications non-covered
210.3.span: All other indications for colorectal cancer screening not otherwise specified in the Act and regulations, or otherwise specified above remain nationally non-covered.

210.7.text: Ages 15-65: one annual voluntary screening without regard to risk
210.7.span: a maximum of one, annual, voluntary screening for all adolescents and adults between the age of 15 and 65, without regard to perceived risk

210.7.text: Under 15 or over 65: one annual screening only if at increased risk (per the NCD's list, including persons who request the test)
210.7.span: a maximum of one, annual, voluntary screening for adolescents younger than 15 and adults older than 65 who are at increased risk for HIV infection

210.7.text: Annual limit: at least 11 full months after the month of the previous test
210.7.span: at least 11 full months must have elapsed following the month in which the previous test was performed in order for the subsequent test to be covered

210.7.text: Pregnancy: up to three screenings, at diagnosis of pregnancy, in the third trimester, and at labor
210.7.span: A maximum of three, voluntary, HIV screenings of pregnant Medicare beneficiaries: (1) when the diagnosis of pregnancy is known, (2) during the third trimester, and, (3) at labor, if ordered by the woman's clinician.

210.7.text: Known diagnosis of HIV-related illness excludes screening
210.7.span: Medicare beneficiaries with any known diagnosis of an HIV-related illness are not eligible for this screening test.

210.7.text: Ordered by the beneficiary's physician or practitioner in a healthcare setting, performed by an eligible Medicare provider
210.7.span: when ordered by the beneficiary's physician or practitioner within the context of a healthcare setting and performed by an eligible Medicare provider for these services

210.7.text: Increased risk determined by the practitioner from the patient's history
210.7.span: The determination of "increased risk" for HIV infection is identified by the health care practitioner who assesses the patient's history

210.12.span: CMS covers intensive behavioral therapy for obesity, defined as a body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m2

210.12.text: Beneficiary competent and alert at the time of counseling
210.12.span: who are competent and alert at the time that counseling is provided

210.12.text: Counseling by a qualified primary care physician or practitioner in a primary care setting
210.12.span: whose counseling is furnished by a qualified primary care physician or other primary care practitioner and in a primary care setting
One face-to-face visit every week for the first month;
One face-to-face visit every other week for months 2-6;

210.12.text: Months 7-12 monthly visits require >= 3 kg weight loss over the first six months
210.12.span: To be eligible for additional face-to-face visits occurring once a month for an additional six months, beneficiaries must have achieved a reduction in weight of at least 3kg over the course of the first six months of intensive therapy.

210.12.text: The 3 kg determination is documented in the physician office records
210.12.span: This determination must be documented in the physician office records for applicable beneficiaries consistent with usual practice.

210.12.text: Settings not considered primary care (ED, inpatient, ASC, IDTF, SNF, IRF, hospice)
210.12.span: Emergency departments, inpatient hospital settings, ambulatory surgical centers, independent diagnostic testing facilities, skilled nursing facilities, inpatient rehabilitation facilities and hospices are not considered primary care settings under this definition.

210.13.text: Ordered by the beneficiary's primary care physician or practitioner within a primary care setting
210.13.span: when ordered by the beneficiary's primary care physician or practitioner within the context of a primary care setting

210.13.text: High risk: current or past illicit injection drug use, or blood transfusion before 1992
210.13.span: "High risk" is defined as persons with a current or past history of illicit injection drug use; and persons who have a history of receiving a blood transfusion prior to 1992.

210.13.text: Annual repeat screening only for continued illicit injection drug use since the prior negative test
210.13.span: Repeat screening for high risk persons is covered annually only for persons who have had continued illicit injection drug use since the prior negative screening test.

210.13.text: Not high risk: single screening test only if born 1945 through 1965
210.13.span: A single screening test is covered for adults who do not meet the high risk definition above, but who were born from 1945 through 1965.

210.13.text: Settings not considered primary care (ED, inpatient, ASC, IDTF, SNF, IRF, limited-focus clinics, hospice)
210.13.span: Emergency departments, inpatient hospital settings, ambulatory surgical centers, independent diagnostic testing facilities, skilled nursing facilities, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, clinics providing a limited focus of health care services, and hospice are examples of settings not considered primary care settings under this definition.

210.13.text: FDA-approved/cleared laboratory tests used per labeling and CLIA
210.13.span: CMS will cover screening for HCV with the appropriate U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved/cleared laboratory tests, used consistent with FDA-approved labeling and in compliance with the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act regulations

210.14.text: Asymptomatic (no signs or symptoms of lung cancer)
210.14.span: Asymptomatic (no signs or symptoms of lung cancer)

210.14.text: Tobacco smoking history of at least 20 pack-years
210.14.span: Tobacco smoking history of at least 20 pack-years (one pack-year = smoking one pack per day for one year; 1 pack =20 cigarettes)

210.14.text: Current smoker or quit within the last 15 years
210.14.span: Current smoker or one who has quit smoking within the last 15 years

210.14.text: Order for lung cancer screening with LDCT
210.14.span: Receive an order for lung cancer screening with LDCT

210.14.text: Before the first screening: counseling and shared decision-making visit (eligibility determination, decision aid, adherence/comorbidity counseling, smoking cessation/abstinence counseling), documented in the medical record
210.14.span: Before the beneficiary's first lung cancer LDCT screening, the beneficiary must receive a counseling and shared decision-making visit that meets all of the following criteria, and is appropriately documented in the beneficiary's medical records

210.14.text: Reading radiologist board-certified or board-eligible (ABR or equivalent)
210.14.span: The reading radiologist must have board certification or board eligibility with the American Board of Radiology or equivalent organization.

210.14.text: Facility uses a standardized lung nodule identification, classification, and reporting system
210.14.span: must be furnished in a radiology imaging facility that utilizes a standardized lung nodule identification, classification, and reporting system

220.6.1.text: Known or suspected coronary artery disease
220.6.1.span: noninvasive imaging of the perfusion of the heart for the diagnosis and management of patients with known or suspected coronary artery disease

220.6.1.text: Performed at rest or with pharmacological stress
220.6.1.span: PET scans performed at rest or with pharmacological stress
using the FDA-approved radiopharmaceutical Rubidium 82 (Rb 82) are covered
using the FDA-approved radiopharmaceutical ammonia N-13 are covered

220.6.1.text: Performed in place of, not in addition to, SPECT
220.6.1.span: The PET scan, whether at rest alone, or rest with stress, is performed in place of, but not in addition to, a single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT)

220.6.1.text: Or following an inconclusive SPECT, where PET is necessary to determine the required medical or surgical intervention
220.6.1.span: The PET scan, whether at rest alone or rest with stress, is used following a SPECT that was found to be inconclusive. In these cases, the PET scan must have been considered necessary in order to determine what medical or surgical intervention is required to treat the patient.

220.6.1.text: Inconclusive = equivocal, technically uninterpretable, or discordant with other clinical data; must be documented in the beneficiary's file
220.6.1.span: an inconclusive test is a test(s) whose results are equivocal, technically uninterpretable, or discordant with a patient's other clinical data and must be documented in the beneficiary's file

220.6.13.text: Recent dementia diagnosis, documented cognitive decline >= 6 months, meets diagnostic criteria for both AD and FTD
220.6.13.span: in patients with a recent diagnosis of dementia and documented cognitive decline of at least 6 months, who meet diagnostic criteria for both AD and FTD

220.6.13.text: Onset, presentation or course makes FTD a suspected alternative cause
220.6.13.span: The patient's onset, clinical presentation, or course of cognitive impairment is such that FTD is suspected as an alternative neurodegenerative cause of the cognitive decline.

220.6.13.text: Comprehensive clinical evaluation: history from patient and informant incl. ADLs, physical and mental status exam with cognitive scales or neuropsychological testing, labs, structural imaging (MRI/CT)
220.6.13.span: The patient has had a comprehensive clinical evaluation (as defined by the American Academy of Neurology encompassing a medical history from the patient and a well-acquainted informant (including assessment of activities of daily living), physical and mental status examination (including formal documentation of cognitive decline occurring over at least 6 months) aided by cognitive scales or neuropsychological testing, laboratory tests, and structural imaging such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT)

220.6.13.text: Evaluation by a physician experienced in diagnosing dementia
220.6.13.span: The evaluation of the patient has been conducted by a physician experienced in the diagnosis and assessment of dementia

220.6.13.text: Evaluation did not clearly determine the cause; PET expected to clarify FTD vs AD and guide treatment
220.6.13.span: The evaluation of the patient did not clearly determine a specific neurodegenerative disease or other cause for the clinical symptoms, and information available through FDG PET is reasonably expected to help clarify the diagnosis between FTD and AD and help guide future treatment

220.6.13.text: Facility has all accreditation needed to operate nuclear medicine equipment; read by experienced expert
220.6.13.span: The FDG PET scan is performed in a facility that has all the accreditation necessary to operate nuclear medicine equipment.

220.6.13.text: No prior brain SPECT or FDG PET for the same indication (unless the repeat exception applies)
220.6.13.span: A brain single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) or FDG PET scan has not been obtained for the same indication.

220.6.13.text: Repeat exception: prior scan inconclusive, important change in scope/severity, and at least one year since the first scan
220.6.13.span: In these instances, an FDG PET scan may be covered after one year has passed from the time the first SPECT or FDG PET scan was performed.

220.6.13.text: Medical record contains required items: onset date, syndrome diagnosis, MMSE or similar score, presumptive cause, neuropsychological testing, structural imaging results, B12/thyroid labs, number and names of medications
220.6.13.span: Providers should establish the medical necessity of an FDG PET scan by ensuring that the following information has been collected and is maintained in the beneficiary medical record

220.6.13.text: MCI or early dementia outside B.1 circumstances: covered only in a CMS-approved clinical trial
220.6.13.span: An FDG PET scan is considered reasonable and necessary in patients with MCI or early dementia (in clinical circumstances other than those specified in subparagraph 1) only in the context of an approved clinical trial

220.6.13.text: All other uses for presumptive dementia diagnoses (e.g., probable AD, clinically typical FTD) non-covered
220.6.13.span: All other uses of FDG PET for patients with a presumptive diagnosis of dementia-causing neurodegenerative disease (e.g., possible or probable AD, clinically typical FTD, dementia of Lewy bodies, or Creutzfeld-Jacob disease) for which CMS has not specifically indicated coverage continue to be noncovered.

230.10.text: Skin test for collagen sensitivity administered and evaluated over 4 weeks before therapy
230.10.span: Prior to collagen implant therapy, a skin test for collagen sensitivity must be administered and evaluated over a 4 week period.

230.10.text: Male evaluation: H&P, simple cystometrogram, standing full-bladder stress leak establishing ISD
230.10.span: In male patients, the evaluation must include a complete history and physical examination and a simple cystometrogram to determine that the bladder fills and stores properly.

230.10.text: Female evaluation: H&P with pelvic exam and simple cystometrogram, then abdominal leak point pressure
230.10.span: In female patients, the evaluation must include a complete history and physical examination (including a pelvic exam) and a simple cystometrogram to rule out abnormalities of bladder compliance and abnormalities of urethral support.

230.10.text: Physician has urology training in cystoscopy and completed a collagen implant training program
230.10.span: physicians must have urology training in the use of a cystoscope and must complete a collagen implant training program

230.10.text: Male patients following trauma, including prostatectomy and/or radiation
230.10.span: Male patients following trauma, including prostatectomy and/or radiation

230.10.text: Female patients without urethral hypermobility and with ALPP of 100 cm H2O or less
230.10.span: Female patients without urethral hypermobility and with abdominal leak point pressures of 100 cm H2O or less.

230.10.text: No further coverage after 5 injection sessions without improvement (treatment failure)
230.10.span: Patients whose incontinence does not improve with 5 injection procedures (5 separate treatment sessions) are considered treatment failures, and no further treatment of urinary incontinence by collagen implant is covered.

230.10.text: Additional sessions after recurrence following past successful treatment, with medical justification
230.10.span: Patients who have a reoccurrence of incontinence following successful treatment with collagen implants in the past (e.g., 6-12 months previously) may benefit from additional treatment sessions. Coverage of additional sessions may be allowed but must be supported by medical justification.

240.1.span: Stable with ≤ 20 mg prednisone (or equivalent) qd

240.1.text: Cardiologist approval if unstable angina, LVEF not estimable, non-sinus rhythm, PVCs, etc.
240.1.span: Approval for surgery by cardiologist if any of the following are present

240.1.text: Post-rehabilitation approval by pulmonary physician, thoracic surgeon, and anesthesiologist
240.1.span: Approval for surgery by pulmonary physician, thoracic surgeon, and anesthesiologist post-rehabilitation

240.1.text: Plasma cotinine <= 13.7 ng/mL (or carboxyhemoglobin <= 2.5% if using nicotine products)
240.1.span: Plasma cotinine level ≤13.7 ng/mL (or arterial carboxyhemoglobin ≤ 2.5% if using nicotine products)

240.1.text: Nonsmoking for 4 months before the initial interview and throughout evaluation
240.1.span: Nonsmoking for 4 months prior to initial interview and throughout evaluation for surgery

240.1.text: Severe upper-lobe-predominant emphysema, or severe non-upper-lobe emphysema with low exercise capacity (<= 25 W women, <= 40 W men)
240.1.span: Patients with low exercise capacity are those whose maximal exercise capacity is at or below 25 watts for women and 40 watts (w) for men

240.1.text: Excluded: non-upper-lobe emphysema with high exercise capacity (> 25 W women, > 40 W men)
240.1.span: has severe, non-upper lobe emphysema with high exercise capacity

240.1.text: Excluded: FEV1 <= 20% predicted with homogeneous emphysema or DLCO <= 20% predicted
240.1.span: The patient presents with FEV1 ≤ 20% of predicted value, and either homogeneous distribution of emphysema on CT scan, or carbon monoxide diffusing capacity of ≤ 20% of predicted value

240.1.text: Facility: Joint Commission LVRS Disease Specific Care certified, or Medicare-approved lung/heart-lung transplant hospital
240.1.span: certified by the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations (Joint Commission) under the LVRS Disease Specific Care Certification Program

240.1.text: Preoperative program: 16-20 sessions over 6-10 weeks, each >= 2 hours
240.1.span: The program must include a 6- to 10-week series of at least 16, and no more than 20, preoperative sessions, each lasting a minimum of 2 hours.

240.1.text: Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation
240.1.span: Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation

240.2.text: Initial claim based on a clinical test ordered and evaluated by the treating practitioner
240.2.span: Initial claims for oxygen therapy for hypoxemic patients must be based on the results of a clinical test that has been ordered and evaluated by the treating practitioner.

240.2.text: Group I: PaO2 <= 55 mm Hg or SaO2 <= 88% at rest on room air
240.2.span: An arterial PO2 at or below 55 mm Hg, or an arterial oxygen saturation at or below 88%, taken at rest, breathing room air

240.2.text: Group II: PaO2 56-59 or SaO2 89% with edema suggesting CHF, pulmonary hypertension/cor pulmonale, or hematocrit > 56%
240.2.span: Coverage is available for patients whose arterial PO2 is 56-59 mm Hg or whose arterial blood oxygen saturation is 89%, if there is:

240.2.text: Inpatients: qualifying test within 2 days of discharge
240.2.span: For an inpatient hospital patient the time of need is within 2 days of discharge.

240.2.text: When ABG and oximetry conflict, ABG is preferred
240.2.span: When the arterial blood gas and the oximetry studies are both used to document the need for home oxygen therapy and the results are conflicting, the arterial blood gas study is the preferred source of documenting medical need.
Angina pectoris in the absence of hypoxemia.

240.2.text: Non-covered: breathlessness without cor pulmonale or evidence of hypoxemia
240.2.span: Breathlessness without cor pulmonale or evidence of hypoxemia.

240.2.text: Non-covered: severe PVD with desaturation in an extremity
240.2.span: Severe peripheral vascular disease resulting in clinically evident desaturation in one or more extremities.

240.2.text: Non-covered: terminal illness unless it affects the ability to breathe
240.2.span: Terminal illnesses unless they affect the ability to breathe.

240.4.span: The use of CPAP is covered under Medicare when used in adult patients with OSA

240.4.text: Provider educates the beneficiary on proper device use before use (a consistently available, willing and able caregiver may compensate)
240.4.span: The provider of CPAP must conduct education of the beneficiary prior to the use of the CPAP device to ensure that the beneficiary has been educated in the proper use of the device
A positive diagnosis of OSA for the coverage of CPAP must include a clinical evaluation

240.4.text: Positive attended PSG, or unattended HST with Type II, Type III, or Type IV (at least 3 channels) device
240.4.span: attended PSG performed in a sleep laboratory; or unattended HST with a Type II home sleep monitoring device; or unattended HST with a Type III home sleep monitoring device; or unattended HST with a Type IV home sleep monitoring device that measures at least 3 channels

240.4.text: Sleep test ordered by the treating physician and furnished under appropriate physician supervision
240.4.span: The sleep test must have been previously ordered by the beneficiary's treating physician and furnished under appropriate physician supervision

240.4.text: AHI/RDI >= 15, or 5-14 with documented excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorder, insomnia, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke
240.4.span: AHI or RDI greater than or equal to 15 events per hour, or AHI or RDI greater than or equal to 5 events and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with documented symptoms of excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders or insomnia, or documented hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke

240.4.text: If under 2 hours of continuous recorded sleep, total events must be at least the number required in a 2-hour period
240.4.span: If the AHI or RDI is calculated based on less than 2 hours of continuous recorded sleep, the total number of recorded events to calculate the AHI or RDI during sleep testing must be at a minimum the number of events that would have been required in a 2-hour period

240.4.text: Initial coverage limited to 12 weeks; continued coverage only if the beneficiary benefits from CPAP during that period
240.4.span: Coverage of CPAP is initially limited to a 12-week period to identify beneficiaries diagnosed with OSA as subsequently described who benefit from CPAP. CPAP is subsequently covered only for those beneficiaries diagnosed with OSA who benefit from CPAP during this 12-week period

240.4.text: Other diagnostic tests (not listed) are not sufficient for CPAP coverage
240.4.span: other diagnostic tests for the diagnosis of OSA, other than those noted above for prescribing CPAP, are not sufficient for the coverage of CPAP

240.9.text: Awake PaCO2 >= 52 mmHg on ABG while on prescribed FiO2
240.9.span: The patient exhibits persistent hypercapnia as demonstrated by PaCO2 ≥ 52 mmHg by arterial blood gas during awake hours while breathing his/her prescribed FiO2

240.9.text: Sleep apnea not the predominant cause of hypercapnia (formal sleep test not required if the clinician so determines)
240.9.span: Sleep apnea is not the predominant cause of the hypercapnia

240.9.text: RAD with backup rate: stable COPD (no >1 worsening symptom >= 2 days and no medication change in prior 2 weeks) or hypercapnia >= 2 weeks after an exacerbation requiring acute NIV
240.9.span: Stable COPD, without increase in or new onset of more than one respiratory symptom (cough, sputum production, sputum purulence, wheezing, or dyspnea) lasting 2 or more days and no change of pharmacological treatment during the 2-week period before initiation of NIV

240.9.text: At discharge: required RAD or ventilator in the 24 h before discharge and clinician documents risk of rapid worsening
240.9.span: if the patient required either a RAD or ventilator within the 24-hour period prior to hospital discharge and the treating clinician determines that the patient is at risk of rapid symptom exacerbation or rise in PaCO2 after discharge

240.9.text: Continued RAD coverage (first evaluation by 6 months): use >= 4 h per 24 h on >= 70% of days in a 30-day period
240.9.span: the patient must be determined by a clinician to use the RAD at least 4 hours per 24-hour period, on at least 70% of days in a 30-day period

240.9.text: Continued RAD coverage: at least one outcome (PaCO2 normalization, stabilization of rising PaCO2, 20% reduction, or improved hypercapnia symptom)
240.9.span: 20% reduction in PaCO2 from baseline value

240.9.text: Home mechanical ventilator: additionally needs FiO2 >= 36% or >= 4 L O2, > 8 h/day support, alarms/battery need, or needs exceeding a RAD
240.9.span: Requires oxygen therapy at an FiO2 ≥ 36% or ≥ 4L nasally

260.1.text: End-stage liver disease other than malignancy (hepatitis B no longer excluded since Dec 10, 1999) in a CMS-approved facility
260.1.span: adult liver transplantation when performed on beneficiaries with end-stage liver disease other than malignancies is covered under Medicare when performed in a facility which is approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria

260.1.text: HCC: patient not a candidate for subtotal liver resection
260.1.span: The patient is not a candidate for subtotal liver resection
The patient's tumor(s) is less than or equal to 5 cm in diameter

260.1.text: HCC: no identifiable extrahepatic spread to lymph nodes, lungs, abdominal organs or bone
260.1.span: There is no identifiable extrahepatic spread of tumor to surrounding lymph nodes, lungs, abdominal organs or bone
The transplant is furnished in a facility that is approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria for liver transplants

260.1.text: Re-transplantation required as a result of a covered liver transplant is covered
260.1.span: Follow-up care or re-transplantation required as a result of a covered liver transplant is covered

260.1.text: Other malignancies (not HCC per criteria; CCA/NET/HAE at MAC discretion) excluded
260.1.span: Adult liver transplantation for other malignancies remains excluded from coverage.

260.3.text: Whole-organ pancreas transplant covered simultaneous with or after a kidney transplant
260.3.span: whole organ pancreas transplantation is nationally covered by Medicare when performed simultaneous with or after a kidney transplant

260.3.text: Pancreas alone (PA): facility Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation
260.3.span: PA will be limited to those facilities that are Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation.

260.3.text: PA: type 1 diabetes shown by beta cell autoantibody positivity or insulinopenia (fasting C-peptide <= 110% of lab LLN with concurrent fasting glucose <= 225 mg/dL)
260.3.span: Patient must demonstrate insulinopenia defined as a fasting C-peptide level that is less than or equal to 110% of the lower limit of normal of the laboratory's measurement method. Fasting C-peptide levels will only be considered valid with a concurrently obtained fasting glucose ≤ 225 mg/dL

260.3.text: PA: labile diabetes with documented recurrent, severe, acutely life-threatening metabolic complications requiring hospitalization
260.3.span: Patients must have a history of medically-uncontrollable labile (brittle) insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus with documented recurrent, severe, acutely life-threatening metabolic complications that require hospitalization.

260.3.text: PA: optimally and intensively managed by an endocrinologist for at least 12 months with advanced insulin formulations and delivery systems
260.3.span: Patients must have been optimally and intensively managed by an endocrinologist for at least 12 months with the most medically-recognized advanced insulin formulations and delivery systems

260.3.text: PA: emotional and mental capacity to understand surgical risks and manage lifelong immunosuppression
260.3.span: Patients must have the emotional and mental capacity to understand the significant risks associated with surgery and to effectively manage the lifelong need for immunosuppression

260.3.text: Partial pancreatic tissue or islet cell transplantation non-covered outside a clinical trial
260.3.span: Transplantation of partial pancreatic tissue or islet cells (except in the context of a clinical trial

260.9.text: Performed in a Medicare-approved heart transplant facility
260.9.span: Cardiac transplantation is covered under Medicare when performed in a facility which is approved by Medicare as meeting institutional coverage criteria.

260.9.text: No exceptions for programs < 2 years old; consortia not approved
260.9.span: Under no circumstances will exceptions be made for facilities whose transplant programs have been in existence for less than 2 years, and applications from consortia will not be approved.

260.9.text: Pediatric hospital: covered only if CMS approved its application (joint program with an approved facility, shared surgeons/QA, specialized resources)
260.9.span: Cardiac transplantation is covered for Medicare beneficiaries when performed in a pediatric hospital that performs pediatric heart transplants if the hospital submits an application which CMS approves

260.9.text: Follow-up care covered even after a noncovered transplant
260.9.span: Follow-up care is also covered for patients who have been discharged from a hospital after receiving a noncovered heart transplant.

260.9.text: Follow-up care after covered transplant, if reasonable and necessary
260.9.span: Follow-up care required as a result of a covered heart transplant is covered, provided such services are otherwise reasonable and necessary.

280.3.text: Mobility limitation significantly impairs one or more MRADLs in the home
280.3.span: Does the beneficiary have a mobility limitation that significantly impairs his/her ability to participate in one or more MRADLs in the home?

280.3.text: Other limiting conditions (e.g., cognition, vision) can be ameliorated or compensated so MAE will help
280.3.span: If these other limitations exist, can they be ameliorated or compensated sufficiently such that the additional provision of MAE will be reasonably expected to significantly improve the beneficiary’s ability to perform or obtain assistance to participate in MRADLs in the home?

280.3.text: Beneficiary or caregiver demonstrates capability and willingness to operate the MAE safely
280.3.span: Does the beneficiary or caregiver demonstrate the capability and the willingness to consistently operate the MAE safely?

280.3.text: If a cane or walker resolves the deficit, more complex MAE is not appropriate
280.3.span: Can the functional mobility deficit be sufficiently resolved by the prescription of a cane or walker?

280.3.text: Home environment supports use of the wheelchair/POV
280.3.span: Does the beneficiary’s typical environment support the use of wheelchairs including scooters/power-operated vehicles (POVs)?

280.3.text: Manual wheelchair: sufficient upper extremity function to self-propel, or an available, willing, able caregiver
280.3.span: Does the beneficiary have sufficient upper extremity function to propel a manual wheelchair in the home to participate in MRADLs during a typical day?

280.3.text: POV: sufficient strength and postural stability
280.3.span: Does the beneficiary have sufficient strength and postural stability to operate a POV/scooter?

280.3.text: Power wheelchair: its additional features are needed for MRADLs
280.3.span: Are the additional features provided by a power wheelchair needed to allow the beneficiary to participate in one or more MRADLs?

280.3.text: Exception: no trial needed where the condition clearly precludes a device
280.3.span: In individual cases where the beneficiary’s condition clearly and unambiguously precludes the reasonable use of a device, it is not necessary to undertake a trial of that device for that beneficiary.

280.3.text: Caregiver may compensate for inability to self-propel a manual wheelchair
280.3.span: If the beneficiary is unable to self-propel a manual wheelchair, and if there is a caregiver who is available, willing, and able to provide assistance, a manual wheelchair may be appropriate.

280.6.text: Covered only for lymphedema or CVI with venous stasis ulcers
280.6.span: Pneumatic devices are covered for the treatment of lymphedema or for the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency with venous stasis ulcers.

280.6.text: Lymphedema: four-week conservative trial with no significant improvement or significant remaining symptoms
280.6.span: Pneumatic compression devices are covered in the home setting for the treatment of lymphedema if the patient has undergone a four-week trial of conservative therapy and the treating physician determines that there has been no significant improvement or if significant symptoms remain after the trial.

280.6.text: Lymphedema trial includes compression bandage/garment, exercise, and limb elevation
280.6.span: The trial of conservative therapy must include use of an appropriate compression bandage system or compression garment, exercise, and elevation of the limb.

280.6.text: CVI: venous stasis ulcer(s) failed to heal after a 6-month physician-directed conservative trial
280.6.span: only if the patient has one or more venous stasis ulcer(s) which have failed to heal after a 6 month trial of conservative therapy directed by the treating physician.

280.6.text: Physician prescription and oversight (evaluation, instruction, treatment plan, monitoring)
280.6.span: Pneumatic compression devices are covered only when prescribed by a physician and when they are used with appropriate physician oversight

280.6.text: Physician determination includes objective findings with measurements of severity
280.6.span: Symptoms and objective findings, including measurements which establish the severity of the condition;

280.6.text: Physician determination includes clinical response to an initial treatment with the device
280.6.span: The clinical response to an initial treatment with the device.

280.6.text: Segmented calibrated gradient device (E0652) only with unique characteristics preventing satisfactory treatment with simpler devices
280.6.span: The only time that a segmented, calibrated gradient pneumatic compression device (HCPCs code E0652) would be covered is when the individual has unique characteristics that prevent them from receiving satisfactory pneumatic compression treatment using a nonsegmented device in conjunction with a segmented appliance or a segmented compression device without manual control of pressure in each chamber.

280.7.text: Condition requires body positioning not feasible in an ordinary bed
280.7.span: The patient's condition requires positioning of the body; e.g., to alleviate pain, promote good body alignment, prevent contractures, avoid respiratory infections, in ways not feasible in an ordinary bed

280.7.text: Or condition requires special attachments that cannot be used on an ordinary bed
280.7.span: The patient's condition requires special attachments that cannot be fixed and used on an ordinary bed.

280.7.text: Physician's prescription accompanies the initial claim
280.7.span: The physician's prescription, which must accompany the initial claim

280.7.text: Positioning: prescription/documentation describes the condition and the severity and frequency of symptoms
280.7.span: the prescription or other documentation must describe the medical condition, e.g., cardiac disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, quadriplegia or paraplegia, and also the severity and frequency of the symptoms of the condition that necessitates a hospital bed for positioning.

280.7.text: Attachments: prescription describes the condition and specifies the attachments
280.7.span: the prescription must describe the patient's condition and specify the attachments that require a hospital bed.

280.7.text: Variable height only for listed conditions where it assists ambulation, avoids strain getting up/down, or aids transfers
280.7.span: The condition requires the variable height feature to assist the patient to ambulate by enabling the patient to place his or her feet on the floor while sitting on the edge of the bed

280.7.text: Electric adjustments: frequent and/or immediate need for position change
280.7.span: the patient's condition requires frequent change in body position and/or there may be an immediate need for a change in body position (i.e., no delay can be tolerated)

280.7.text: Electric adjustments: patient can operate the controls (exceptions only for SCI and brain damage)
280.7.span: the patient can operate the controls and cause the adjustments. Exceptions may be made to this last requirement in cases of spinal cord injury and brain damaged patients.

280.8.span: The patient has a stage 3 (full thickness tissue loss) or stage 4 (deep tissue destruction) pressure sore;

280.8.text: Bedridden or chair bound from severely limited mobility
280.8.span: The patient is bedridden or chair bound as a result of severely limited mobility;

280.8.text: Would require institutionalization without the bed
280.8.span: In the absence of an air-fluidized bed, the patient would require institutionalization;

280.8.text: Conservative treatment for at least one month without progression toward healing (may include documented institutional time)
280.8.span: This course of treatment must have been at least one month in duration without progression toward wound healing.

280.8.text: Conservative treatment included a Group II specialized support surface
280.8.span: Use of a specialized support surface (Group II) designed to reduce pressure and shear forces on healing ulcers and to prevent new ulcer formation;
A trained adult caregiver is available to assist the patient with activities of daily living

280.8.text: Not covered with coexisting pulmonary disease
280.8.span: The patient has coexisting pulmonary disease

280.8.text: Not covered if wet soaks or moist dressings are not protected by an occlusive covering
280.8.span: The patient requires treatment with wet soaks or moist wound dressings that are not protected with an impervious covering such as plastic wrap or other occlusive material;

280.8.text: Written order from the attending physician furnished to the supplier before delivery
280.8.span: Payment for this covered item may only be made if the written order from the attending physician is furnished to the supplier prior to the delivery of the equipment.

280.8.text: Exception: institutional time may count toward the conservative month if documented
280.8.span: This month of prerequisite conservative treatment may include some period in an institution as long as there is documentation available to verify that the necessary conservative treatment has been rendered.

280.8.text: Exception: wet-to-dry debridement continuing beyond 30 days does not preclude coverage
280.8.span: Use of wet-to-dry dressings for wound debridement, begun during the period of conservative treatment and which continue beyond 30 days, will not preclude coverage of air-fluidized bed.

280.14.text: CSII: insulinopenia (fasting C-peptide <= 110% of LLN) or beta cell autoantibody positive
280.14.span: Insulinopenia is defined as a fasting C-peptide level that is less than or equal to 110% of the lower limit of normal of the laboratory's measurement method.

280.14.text: CSII: with creatinine clearance <= 50 mL/min, insulinopenia threshold is <= 200% of LLN
280.14.span: For patients with renal insufficiency and creatinine clearance (actual or calculated from age, gender, weight, and serum creatinine) ≤ 50 ml/minute, insulinopenia is defined as a fasting C-peptide level that is less than or equal to 200% of the lower limit of normal of the laboratory's measurement method.

280.14.text: CSII Criterion A: diabetes education, MDI >= 3 injections/day with self-adjustment for >= 6 months
280.14.span: The patient has completed a comprehensive diabetes education program, and has been on a program of multiple daily injections of insulin (i.e., at least 3 injections per day), with frequent self-adjustments of insulin doses for at least 6 months prior to initiation of the insulin pump

280.14.text: CSII Criterion A: documented self-testing averaging >= 4 times/day during the 2 months before pump
280.14.span: has documented frequency of glucose self-testing an average of at least 4 times per day during the 2 months prior to initiation of the insulin pump

280.14.text: CSII Criterion A: on MDI, meets >= 1 of HbA1c > 7.0%, recurring hypoglycemia, wide pre-meal fluctuations, dawn phenomenon with FBS often > 200, severe glycemic excursions
280.14.span: meets one or more of the following criteria while on the multiple daily injection regimen

280.14.text: CSII Criterion B: on a pump before Medicare enrollment with self-testing averaging >= 4/day in the month before enrollment
280.14.span: The patient with diabetes has been on a pump prior to enrollment in Medicare and has documented frequency of glucose self-testing an average of at least 4 times per day during the month prior to Medicare enrollment.

280.14.text: CSII ordered and managed by a physician experienced with multiple CSII patients and a CSII team
280.14.span: The pump must be ordered by and follow-up care of the patient must be managed by a physician who manages multiple patients with CSII

280.14.text: Intrathecal antispasmodic pump: >= 6-week trial of non-invasive spasm control failed or not tolerated
280.14.span: As indicated by at least a 6-week trial, the patient cannot be maintained on non-invasive methods of spasm control

280.14.text: Intrathecal antispasmodic pump: favorable response to a trial intrathecal dose before implantation
280.14.span: prior to pump implantation, the patient must have responded favorably to a trial intrathecal dose of the anti-spasmodic drug

280.14.text: Implantable opioid pump: life expectancy >= 3 months
280.14.span: in patients who have a life expectancy of at least 3 months

280.14.text: Implantable opioid pump: preliminary trial with temporary intrathecal/epidural catheter
280.14.span: a preliminary trial of intraspinal opioid drug administration must be undertaken with a temporary intrathecal/epidural catheter

280.14.text: Implantation contraindicated with other implanted programmable devices
280.14.span: With other implanted programmable devices since crosstalk between devices may inadvertently change the prescription.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old man resuscitated from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation. Serial troponins and coronary angiography showed no acute MI and no culprit lesion; electrolytes, drug levels and toxicology were normal and no other transient or reversible cause was found. Echocardiogram LVEF 45%. Requesting an initial ICD. He is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia.
cases.note: Secondary prevention after VF arrest; shared decision making is not required for B1.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy after an anterior MI 2 years ago, NYHA class II heart failure, LVEF 30% on echocardiography. No CABG or PCI in the past year; recent angiography found no lesions suitable for revascularization. No history of sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. She is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
cases.note: Ischemic cardiomyopathy, NYHA II, LVEF 30% by echo, MI 2 years ago.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with a large anterior MI 21 days ago, now with LVEF 25% on echocardiography and NYHA class II symptoms; no revascularization targets remain and no pacemaker indication. No sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD now. He is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
cases.note: MI 21 days ago: inside the 40-day waiting period; no pacemaker indication.

cases.vignette: 55-year-old woman with newly diagnosed non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, LVEF 30% on cardiac MRI, NYHA class III. Normal coronary angiogram. Guideline-directed medical therapy was started 6 weeks ago. No sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. She is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
cases.note: Non-ischemic cardiomyopathy on GDMT for only 6 weeks (needs >= 3 months).

cases.vignette: 61-year-old man with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, LVEF 28% on echocardiography, NYHA class II despite 5 months of optimal medical therapy. Normal coronary angiogram; no sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. The record contains no documentation of a shared decision-making encounter about the ICD. He is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia.
cases.note: Primary prevention without a documented shared decision-making encounter.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, LVEF 25% on echocardiography, NYHA class II, MI 3 years ago, no revascularization options. He was recently diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer; his oncologist estimates survival of 4-6 months. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. He is clinically stable with no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
cases.note: Metastatic pancreatic cancer with expected survival of months.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman who had a ventricular fibrillation arrest with a potassium of 2.1 mmol/L after high-dose diuretic use; potassium was corrected and she has had no further arrhythmia. No acute MI; structurally normal heart with LVEF 60% on echocardiography. Requesting a secondary-prevention ICD. She is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia.
cases.note: VF arrest caused by severe hypokalemia: transient/reversible cause.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old man with an ICD implanted 9 years ago for sustained ventricular tachycardia; the device has reached its elective replacement indicator. LVEF on his latest echocardiogram is 50%. Requesting ICD generator replacement. He is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia.
cases.note: Replacement at ERI; current LVEF 50% and absence of a new SDM encounter do not matter.

cases.vignette: 45-year-old woman with genetically confirmed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, maximal wall thickness 31 mm, unexplained syncope, and a family history of sudden cardiac death; her cardiologist documents high risk of life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia. LVEF 65% on cardiac MRI. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. She is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
cases.note: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: genetic high-risk disorder with SDM.

cases.vignette: 79-year-old man with an MI 4 years ago, LVEF 25% on echocardiography, and NYHA class IV heart failure with symptoms at rest despite therapy; he is not a transplant or LVAD candidate and angiography shows no revascularization targets. No sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. He is not in shock, has no non-cardiac life-limiting disease, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
cases.note: Prior MI with LVEF 25% but NYHA class IV (excluded from B2; B3 also requires NYHA II-III).

cases.vignette: 69-year-old man with CCS class IV stable angina despite maximally tolerated metoprolol, amlodipine, isosorbide mononitrate, and ranolazine. Angiography reviewed by interventional cardiology and cardiac surgery shows diffuse distal disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. LVEF is 40%. PET perfusion-metabolism imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium in the inferolateral wall that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. He has no arrhythmias, heart failure decompensation, or recent infarction. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: CCS IV refractory to maximal therapy, diffuse non-revascularizable disease, EF 40%, PET viability, stable.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old woman with CCS class III angina that became unstable 3 weeks ago; she was hospitalized, treated, and has been clinically stable for 2 weeks on maximally tolerated antianginal therapy, but angina persists. Her LVEF is exactly 25% by echocardiography. Angiography shows diffuse small-vessel disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. Dobutamine stress echocardiography demonstrates viable ischemic myocardium in the anterior wall that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: Boundary: EF exactly 25%; CCS III unstable angina (stable or unstable allowed) after stabilization.

cases.vignette: 82-year-old man with diabetes and two prior coronary bypass operations, now with occluded grafts and native vessels unsuitable for further bypass, angioplasty, stenting, or atherectomy. He has CCS class IV angina despite maximum safe doses of beta blocker, nitrate, calcium channel blocker, and ranolazine. LVEF is 45%. Nuclear viability imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium in the lateral wall not capable of direct revascularization. He is clinically stable. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: Two prior CABGs with failed grafts, age 82, diabetes are not exclusions.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with CCS class II angina (symptoms only with brisk walking uphill) despite maximally tolerated antianginal therapy. Angiography shows diffuse distal disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. LVEF is 50%. Stress perfusion imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. He is clinically stable. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: CCS class II angina; TMR requires class III or IV.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with CCS class IV angina despite maximally tolerated antianginal therapy. Angiography shows diffuse disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. Her LVEF is 20% by cardiac MRI. Viability imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. She is clinically stable. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: LVEF 20%, below the 25% minimum.

cases.vignette: 65-year-old man with CCS class III angina despite maximally tolerated antianginal therapy. Angiography shows a focal 90% proximal right coronary artery stenosis that interventional cardiology judges amenable to stenting, supplying the ischemic territory. He declines stenting and requests TMR. LVEF is 50%. Stress imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium in the inferior wall. He is clinically stable. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: Culprit lesion is amenable to PCI; patient declined it.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman with CCS class III angina. Her only antianginal medication is metoprolol tartrate 12.5 mg twice daily, which has never been titrated; she has no documented intolerance to higher doses or to other antianginal drugs, which have not been tried. Angiography shows diffuse disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. LVEF is 45%. Viability imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium not capable of direct revascularization. She is clinically stable. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: Medical therapy not at maximum tolerated doses; only low-dose beta blocker, never titrated.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old man with CCS class IV angina despite maximally tolerated antianginal therapy, diffuse disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass, LVEF 30%, and viable ischemic myocardium on PET not capable of direct revascularization. He presented yesterday with decompensated congestive heart failure and pulmonary edema; the team plans TMR tomorrow without first treating or attempting to stabilize the heart failure. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: Currently decompensated heart failure with no attempt at stabilization before TMR.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with CCS class IV angina despite maximally tolerated antianginal therapy. Angiography shows diffuse disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. LVEF is 40%. She is clinically stable. The record contains no stress perfusion, PET, MRI, or other diagnostic study assessing myocardial viability or ischemia. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
cases.note: No diagnostic study demonstrating viable ischemic myocardium in the record.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old man with CCS class IV angina despite maximally tolerated antianginal therapy, diffuse disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass, LVEF 35%, and viable ischemic myocardium on stress perfusion imaging that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. He is clinically stable. The laser is FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization, and the cardiothoracic surgeon completed TMR training. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards. The request contains no documentation of training in the procedure or equipment for the nurses, operating room staff, or technicians.
cases.note: Surgeon trained, but no documentation of ancillary personnel training.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old man with lifestyle-limiting claudication of the right calf. Duplex ultrasound and angiography show an atherosclerotic 85% stenosis of the distal superficial femoral artery extending into the popliteal artery. Balloon angioplasty without stent placement is requested.
cases.note: Atherosclerotic superficial femoral/popliteal lesion: lower-extremity indication.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old woman with left arm claudication and a 30 mmHg inter-arm blood pressure difference. CT angiography shows an atherosclerotic 80% stenosis of the proximal left subclavian artery. She also has a 40% asymptomatic right internal carotid stenosis, which will be managed medically. Balloon angioplasty of the left subclavian artery without stent placement is requested.
cases.note: Subclavian artery is an upper-extremity vessel (not a head/neck vessel) under the NCD.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with angina that persists despite maximally tolerated metoprolol, long-acting nitrate, and ranolazine. A nuclear stress test shows a reversible anterior perfusion defect. Coronary angiography shows a single severe lesion in the proximal left anterior descending artery, judged amenable to angioplasty; the other coronary arteries have no significant disease. The heart team notes that bypass surgery is the likely alternative. Balloon angioplasty of this single coronary artery without stent placement is requested.
cases.note: Single coronary artery; refractory angina; positive stress test; amenable lesion; CABG is the likely alternative.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with an asymptomatic left internal carotid artery stenosis. First-line duplex ultrasound estimated 70-79% stenosis, and CT angiography confirmed 70% stenosis and characterized the aortic arch and intracranial circulation. Carotid PTA concurrent with placement of an FDA-approved carotid stent with an FDA-approved embolic protection device is planned. A neurologist examined him before the procedure and will repeat the assessment afterward. Before scheduling, the interventionalist held a formal shared decision-making visit covering carotid endarterectomy, stenting (including TCAR), and optimal medical therapy, the risks and benefits of each for him, guideline considerations given his comorbidities, and his preferences. The hospital runs a dedicated carotid stent program with a privileging and outcome-monitoring committee, trained staff, appropriate imaging and emergency support, and continuous quality improvement.
cases.note: Boundary: asymptomatic carotid stenosis exactly 70%; all CAS process requirements met.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with recurrent vertebrobasilar transient ischemic attacks despite dual antiplatelet therapy and a statin. CT angiography shows an atherosclerotic 80% stenosis at the origin of the dominant left vertebral artery. Balloon angioplasty of the vertebral artery without stent placement is requested outside of any clinical trial.
cases.note: Vertebral artery PTA is non-covered.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with a 75% atherosclerotic stenosis of the left middle cerebral artery and recurrent strokes in that territory despite aggressive medical therapy. Intracranial balloon angioplasty with stent placement is requested as standard care; the hospital is not participating in any FDA Category B IDE clinical trial of intracranial stenting.
cases.note: Intracranial PTA/stenting outside a Category B IDE trial.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with intracranial atherosclerotic disease and a 40% stenosis of the basilar artery. She is enrolled in an FDA-approved Category B IDE clinical trial of intracranial angioplasty and stenting, and the procedure would follow the trial protocol.
cases.note: In a Category B IDE trial, but stenosis 40% is below the 50% threshold.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old man with atherosclerotic 70% right renal artery stenosis found on imaging. His blood pressure is at goal on two antihypertensive agents and his renal function is stable. His nephrologist states that surgical revascularization is not under consideration. Balloon angioplasty of the renal artery without stent placement is requested in addition to continued medical management.
cases.note: Renal PTA as an add-on to effective medical management; surgery not the likely alternative.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old man with angina refractory to maximally tolerated antianginal therapy and a positive exercise stress echocardiogram. Angiography shows severe lesions in the left anterior descending, left circumflex, and right coronary arteries, all judged amenable to angioplasty; bypass surgery is the likely alternative. Balloon angioplasty without stent placement of all three coronary arteries is requested.
cases.note: Coronary PTA covered only for a single coronary artery; three vessels requested.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old woman with angina that persists despite maximally tolerated beta blocker, nitrate, and calcium channel blocker therapy. Angiography shows a single severe right coronary artery lesion amenable to angioplasty, with no other significant disease; bypass surgery is the likely alternative. The record contains no stress test, fractional flow reserve, or other objective test of myocardial ischemia. Balloon angioplasty of the right coronary artery without stent placement is requested.
cases.note: Single-vessel coronary PTA without any documented objective evidence of ischemia.

cases.vignette: 75-year-old man with an atherosclerotic 85% left renal artery stenosis. The vascular surgeon's note states that surgical renal revascularization is the likely alternative. The record does not document what antihypertensive or other medical management has been tried or how he responded. Balloon angioplasty of the renal artery without stent placement is requested.
cases.note: Surgery is the likely alternative, but no documentation of the medical management tried or the response.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy, NYHA class IV symptoms, and LVEF 15% by echocardiography. He has been on guideline-based optimal medical management for 58 of the last 60 days without response and is dependent on continuous milrinone after two failed weaning attempts. He is not a transplant candidate. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy).
