The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: NYHA IV, LVEF 15%, inotrope dependent, OMM 58/60 days failing; full team, credentialed facility.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, NYHA class IV, LVEF 25% by cardiac MRI. She has been on guideline-based optimal medical management for 45 of the last 60 days and is failing to respond, and she is dependent on continuous dobutamine. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted exactly 10 durable intracorporeal LVADs over the previous 36 months, 2 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: Boundaries: LVEF exactly 25%, OMM exactly 45 of last 60 days, surgeon exactly 10 LVADs in 36 months with 2 in the last year.

cases.vignette: 58-year-old man listed for heart transplant with NYHA class IV heart failure and LVEF 10%. He has had advanced heart failure for 20 days, has been dependent on an intra-aortic balloon pump for the last 9 days, and requires continuous milrinone. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for short-term mechanical circulatory support as a bridge to transplant. The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: IABP branch: advanced HF for 20 days and IABP-dependent for 9 days; bridge to transplant.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old woman who underwent aortic valve replacement and coronary bypass surgery today and could not be weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass despite inotropes. Her pre-operative LVEF was 35% and she had NYHA class II symptoms. The surgeon requests a temporary VAD that is FDA approved for post-cardiotomy circulatory support, to be used according to its FDA-approved labeling. The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: Post-cardiotomy indication: device FDA approved for post-cardiotomy support per labeling. LVEF 35% and NYHA criteria apply to the LVAD heart failure indication, not this one.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with dilated cardiomyopathy, LVEF 18%, and NYHA class III symptoms; he walks one block before stopping and has no symptoms at rest. He is on continuous outpatient milrinone and has been on optimal medical management for all of the last 60 days. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: NYHA class III, not IV.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman with NYHA class IV heart failure and LVEF 30% on two echocardiograms. She is inotrope dependent and has been on optimal medical management for 52 of the last 60 days without response. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: LVEF 30% exceeds the 25% threshold.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with NYHA class IV heart failure, LVEF 14%, inotrope dependent, and on optimal medical management for 50 of the last 60 days without response. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The program's only cardiothoracic surgeon with implant privileges has implanted 7 durable intracorporeal LVADs over the previous 36 months, 3 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: The team's only implanting surgeon has 7 LVADs in 36 months (needs >= 10).

cases.vignette: 69-year-old woman with NYHA class IV heart failure, LVEF 17%, inotrope dependent, and on optimal medical management for 55 of the last 60 days without response. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD care, a VAD program coordinator, and a social worker; the program has no palliative care specialist on the team. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: Team lacks a palliative care specialist.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old man with NYHA class IV heart failure, LVEF 12%, inotrope dependent, and on optimal medical management for 60 of the last 60 days without response. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital's LVAD credential from a CMS-approved organization lapsed 8 months ago and has not been renewed; it is not currently credentialed.
cases.note: Facility credentialing lapsed; not credentialed by a CMS-approved organization.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with NYHA class IV heart failure, dependent on continuous milrinone, and on optimal medical management for 49 of the last 60 days without response. The record describes 'severely reduced systolic function' but contains no echocardiogram, MRI, or other report giving a measured LVEF. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management before and after implant, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by a CMS-approved credentialing organization.
cases.note: No LVEF measurement in the record.

cases.vignette: 65-year-old man with NYHA class IV heart failure, LVEF 16%, inotrope dependent, and on optimal medical management for 54 of the last 60 days without response. The requested device is a durable LVAD FDA approved for long-term mechanical circulatory support (destination therapy). The implanting cardiothoracic surgeon has implanted 34 durable intracorporeal LVADs in the previous 36 months, 11 of them in the last year. The facility-based VAD team includes an advanced heart failure cardiologist experienced in VAD management, a VAD program coordinator, a social worker, and a palliative care specialist. The request contains no information on whether the hospital is credentialed as an LVAD facility by any organization.
cases.note: Facility credentialing status not documented; nothing indicates it is lacking.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and a plantar forefoot ulcer due to diabetic neuropathy, classified Wagner grade III (deep abscess). For the past 6 weeks standard wound care has included vascular assessment (adequate perfusion, no correctable vascular disease), optimization of nutrition and glucose control, serial sharp debridement, moist dressings maintaining a clean granulation bed, total-contact cast off-loading, and treatment of infection; serial measurements show no measurable signs of healing over that period. HBO therapy in a multiplace chamber is requested as an adjunct, with standard wound care continuing and wound re-evaluation at least every 30 days.
cases.note: Type 2 DM, Wagner III foot ulcer, 6 weeks of standard care without measurable healing; HBO in chamber adjunctive to ongoing wound care.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes and a heel ulcer due to diabetes, classified Wagner grade III. For exactly 30 consecutive days standard wound care has included vascular assessment (adequate perfusion, no correctable vascular disease), optimization of nutrition and glucose control, serial sharp debridement, moist dressings maintaining a clean granulation bed, total-contact cast off-loading, and treatment of infection, with weekly measurements showing no measurable signs of healing during those 30 days. Adjunctive HBO therapy in a monoplace chamber is requested, in addition to continued standard wound care, with wound evaluation at least every 30 days.
cases.note: Boundaries: Wagner grade III exactly; exactly 30 consecutive days without measurable healing.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman brought to the emergency department 2 hours after exposure to a malfunctioning furnace, with headache, confusion, and a carboxyhemoglobin level of 28%. She has type 2 diabetes. HBO therapy in a monoplace chamber is requested for acute carbon monoxide intoxication.
cases.note: Acute CO intoxication in a monoplace (one-man) chamber; diabetic-wound criteria irrelevant.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old man treated with radiation for oropharyngeal cancer 3 years ago, now with osteoradionecrosis of the mandible confirmed on imaging. He is receiving conventional treatment including surgical debridement, antibiotics, and oral care. HBO therapy in a multiplace chamber is requested as an adjunct to this conventional treatment.
cases.note: Osteoradionecrosis as an adjunct to conventional treatment.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and a neuropathic plantar ulcer due to diabetes, classified Wagner grade II (deep to tendon, no abscess or osteomyelitis). For 8 weeks standard wound care has included vascular assessment (adequate perfusion, no correctable vascular disease), optimization of nutrition and glucose control, serial sharp debridement, moist dressings maintaining a clean granulation bed, total-contact cast off-loading, and treatment of infection, with no measurable signs of healing. Adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber is requested with continued standard wound care.
cases.note: Wagner grade II; requires grade III or higher.

cases.vignette: 79-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and a stage 4 sacral pressure ulcer after a prolonged hospitalization. The wound has shown no measurable improvement after 10 weeks of debridement, negative-pressure wound therapy, nutrition optimization, glucose control, and pressure off-loading. HBO therapy in a multiplace chamber is requested as an adjunct to wound care.
cases.note: Decubitus (pressure) ulcer is explicitly non-covered, even though the patient has diabetes.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and a Wagner grade IV forefoot wound due to diabetes. He began adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber 35 days ago after 6 weeks of standard wound care without measurable healing, and standard care has continued. Wound evaluations 30 days apart during HBO show identical wound dimensions and no measurable signs of healing. Continuation of HBO therapy for another 30 days is requested.
cases.note: No measurable healing during the last 30-day period of HBO; continued treatment is not covered.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and a Wagner grade III foot ulcer due to diabetes, discovered 16 days ago. Since then she has had debridement, off-loading, moist dressings, glucose optimization, and treatment of infection. The wound surgeon requests adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber now to accelerate healing, in addition to standard wound care.
cases.note: Only 2 weeks of standard wound care before HBO; requires >= 30 days without measurable healing.

cases.vignette: 76-year-old man with long-standing peripheral artery disease and chronic ischemic rest pain in the left foot, with no open wound and no acute change. He is not a candidate for revascularization. HBO therapy in a multiplace chamber is requested to improve tissue oxygenation for his chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency.
cases.note: Chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency is explicitly non-covered (acute peripheral arterial insufficiency would be covered).

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and a plantar foot ulcer due to diabetes measuring 2.5 x 2.0 cm. For 7 weeks standard wound care has included vascular assessment (adequate perfusion, no correctable vascular disease), optimization of nutrition and glucose control, serial sharp debridement, moist dressings maintaining a clean granulation bed, total-contact cast off-loading, and treatment of infection, with no measurable signs of healing. The record does not give a Wagner grade or describe wound depth or whether tendon, bone, or abscess is involved. Adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber is requested with continued standard wound care.
cases.note: Wound severity not documented; no Wagner grade or depth recorded.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and a Wagner grade III ulcer of the lateral foot due to diabetes, which the referral says has been present for 3 months. The record contains no wound care notes, measurements, or description of the standard wound therapy provided during that time. Adjunctive HBO therapy in a chamber is requested.
cases.note: Wound present for months, but no documentation of the standard wound care given or wound measurements.

cases.vignette: 81-year-old woman with exertional dyspnea and angina (NYHA class III). Echocardiogram: severe aortic stenosis, valve area 0.7 cm2, mean gradient 48 mmHg, LVEF 55%. The planned valve system has FDA premarket approval and will be used for its FDA-approved indication. A cardiac surgeon and an interventional cardiologist each independently examined the patient face to face, evaluated suitability for SAVR, TAVR, or medical/palliative therapy, and documented their rationale in the shared record. Both will jointly participate in the procedure. The hospital has on-site heart valve surgery and interventional cardiology programs and a cardiovascular ICU; last year it performed 140 aortic valve replacements including 90 TAVRs, has 4 cardiac surgeons and 3 interventional cardiologists, and performs about 600 PCIs per year. The heart team and hospital participate in a prospective, national, audited TAVR registry.
cases.note: Typical symptomatic severe AS.

cases.vignette: 76-year-old man with mild exertional dyspnea. Echocardiogram: moderate aortic stenosis, valve area 1.3 cm2, mean gradient 25 mmHg, LVEF 60%. The valve system's FDA-approved indication is severe aortic stenosis, and he is not enrolled in any clinical study. A cardiac surgeon and an interventional cardiologist each independently examined the patient face to face, evaluated suitability for SAVR, TAVR, or medical/palliative therapy, and documented their rationale in the shared record. Both will jointly participate in the procedure. The hospital has on-site heart valve surgery and interventional cardiology programs and a cardiovascular ICU; last year it performed 140 aortic valve replacements including 90 TAVRs, has 4 cardiac surgeons and 3 interventional cardiologists, and performs about 600 PCIs per year. cases.vignette: 72-year-old woman with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, LVEF 38%, and NYHA class III symptoms. The patient is enrolled in a CMS-approved CED study of CCM.
cases.note: Boundary: optimized GDMT for exactly 3 months, as determined by the heart team.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old woman with 24-hour ambulatory monitoring showing daytime average 158/96 mm Hg. On lifestyle modification and stable maximally tolerated doses of four antihypertensives (including a diuretic and spironolactone) for 4 months, with adherence confirmed by pharmacy refill records and pill counts. Screening was negative for primary aldosteronism (normal aldosterone-renin ratio), obstructive sleep apnea (home sleep test), and drug- or alcohol-induced hypertension. Her primary care physician has co-managed her blood pressure for 14 months with five encounters, four in person. The planned FDA market-authorized RDN device will be used per its labeled indication. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved CED study. The operator is an interventional cardiologist with active endovascular experience who completed five proctored cases with this device; the facility runs a hypertension program with a hypertension navigator and specialist access, has CT angiography, and a cardiac catheterization lab. Referral is by the primary care physician who manages the patient's hypertension longitudinally. Renal CT angiography shows anatomy suitable for RDN and there are no contraindications in the device labeling. No prior RDN.
cases.note: Typical qualifying resistant hypertension.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old man with bilateral, progressive, post-linguistic sensorineural hearing loss (ICD-10-CM H90.3), moderate-to-profound on audiometry in both ears. He has worn properly fitted bilateral hearing aids for 8 years. On recorded open-set sentence recognition testing in the best-aided condition, he scores 60% correct. A unilateral cochlear implant is requested. Cognitive screening is normal; he understands the device and has committed in writing to the extended auditory rehabilitation program. Otoscopy and tympanometry are normal with no middle ear infection, and temporal bone CT and MRI show normally formed, patent cochleae and normal auditory nerves with no central auditory lesions. Anesthesia evaluation finds no contraindication to surgery, and the planned implant will be used in accordance with its FDA-approved labeling.
cases.note: Boundary: best-aided open-set sentence score exactly 60% meets the <= 60% definition.

cases.vignette: 89-year-old woman with bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss present since early childhood (pre-linguistic, ICD-10-CM H90.3) who has used bilateral hearing aids throughout life with diminishing benefit. Recorded open-set sentence recognition in the best-aided condition is 38% correct. Cochlear implantation in the right ear is requested. Cognitive screening is normal; she understands the device and has committed in writing to the extended auditory rehabilitation program. Otoscopy and tympanometry are normal with no middle ear infection, and temporal bone CT and MRI show normally formed, patent cochleae and normal auditory nerves with no central auditory lesions. Anesthesia evaluation finds no contraindication to surgery, and the planned implant will be used in accordance with its FDA-approved labeling.
cases.note: Score 38%; advanced age (89) and pre-linguistic onset are not exclusions under this NCD.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old man with bilateral moderate-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss (ICD-10-CM H90.3) using bilateral hearing aids for 5 years. He reports difficulty in restaurants. On recorded open-set sentence recognition in the best-aided listening condition he scores 64% correct; word scores are lower at 44%. A cochlear implant is requested. Cognitive screening is normal; he understands the device and has committed in writing to the extended auditory rehabilitation program. Otoscopy and tympanometry are normal with no middle ear infection, and temporal bone CT and MRI show normally formed, patent cochleae and normal auditory nerves with no central auditory lesions. Anesthesia evaluation finds no contraindication to surgery, and the planned implant will be used in accordance with its FDA-approved labeling.
cases.note: Best-aided sentence score 64% exceeds 60%: not 'limited benefit'.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with sudden profound sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear 1 year ago (ICD-10-CM H90.42) and normal hearing thresholds in the right ear. A hearing aid trial in the left ear gave no useful benefit; aided open-set sentence recognition in the left ear alone is 8% correct. Cochlear implantation in the left ear is requested. Cognitive screening is normal; she understands the device and has committed in writing to the extended auditory rehabilitation program. Otoscopy and tympanometry are normal with no middle ear infection, and temporal bone CT and MRI show normally formed, patent cochleae and normal auditory nerves with no central auditory lesions. Anesthesia evaluation finds no contraindication to surgery, and the planned implant will be used in accordance with its FDA-approved labeling.
cases.note: Single-sided deafness: hearing loss is not bilateral.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss (ICD-10-CM H90.3) using bilateral hearing aids, with best-aided recorded open-set sentence recognition of 22% correct. Cognitive screening is normal and he has committed to the rehabilitation program. Otoscopy today shows active chronic suppurative otitis media of the right ear, the ear selected for implantation, with purulent otorrhea; cultures are pending and surgery is to be scheduled now. Imaging shows patent cochleae and normal auditory nerves, there is no contraindication to anesthesia, and the device will be used per FDA-approved labeling.
cases.note: Active middle ear infection in the ear to be implanted.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old man with bilateral moderate-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss (ICD-10-CM H90.3), best-aided recorded open-set sentence recognition 30% correct with bilateral hearing aids. Cognitive screening is normal. During counseling he states he will not attend auditory rehabilitation or device programming visits after activation and expects the device to work on its own; the audiologist documents his refusal of the rehabilitation program. Otoscopy and tympanometry are normal, imaging shows patent cochleae and normal auditory nerves, there is no contraindication to surgery, and the device will be used per FDA-approved labeling.
cases.note: Patient declines the extended rehabilitation program.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with bilateral moderate-to-severe sensorineural hearing loss (ICD-10-CM H90.3) using bilateral hearing aids, with best-aided recorded open-set sentence recognition of 72% correct. She is enrolled in an FDA-approved category B investigational device exemption (IDE) clinical trial studying cochlear implantation for patients with better aided speech scores, and the implant will be placed under that trial protocol. Cognitive screening is normal; she understands the device and has committed in writing to the extended auditory rehabilitation program. Otoscopy and tympanometry are normal with no middle ear infection, and temporal bone CT and MRI show normally formed, patent cochleae and normal auditory nerves with no central auditory lesions. Anesthesia evaluation finds no contraindication to surgery,.
cases.note: Exception (Section D): fails the 60% criterion, but implanted within an FDA-approved category B IDE clinical trial.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old man with bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss on pure-tone audiometry (ICD-10-CM H90.3) who has worn bilateral hearing aids for 10 years and reports that they no longer help. The audiology report includes unaided pure-tone thresholds only; no aided speech or sentence recognition testing was performed or recorded. A cochlear implant is requested. cases.note: No aided speech recognition testing is documented, so limited benefit cannot be established.

cases.vignette: 76-year-old woman with bilateral moderate-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss (ICD-10-CM H90.3) using bilateral hearing aids, with best-aided recorded open-set sentence recognition of 41% correct. Cognitive screening is normal and she has committed to the extended rehabilitation program. There is no contraindication to surgery, and the device will be used per FDA-approved labeling. The submitted record contains the audiology report only; there is no otoscopic examination, no tympanometry, and no CT or MRI of the temporal bones or auditory nerves.
cases.note: No otologic examination or imaging documenting middle ear status, cochlear lumen, or auditory nerve.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old man with bilateral moderate-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss (ICD-10-CM H90.3), best-aided recorded open-set sentence recognition 26% correct with bilateral hearing aids. Cognitive screening is normal and he has committed to rehabilitation. Otoscopy and tympanometry are normal. MRI shows a 9 mm left vestibular schwannoma involving the internal auditory canal and cochlear nerve; the left ear is the one planned for implantation, and the tumor will be observed rather than treated. There is no contraindication to surgery, and the device will be used per FDA-approved labeling.
cases.note: Imaging shows a vestibular schwannoma (auditory nerve lesion) on the side planned for implantation.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old man with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E11.42) and diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Testing with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament at five plantar sites per foot, in random order and avoiding callused areas, shows absent sensation at 2 of 5 sites on the left foot and 1 of 5 on the right, documented in the note. His last foot evaluation for diabetic neuropathy with LOPS was 7 months ago, and he has not seen a podiatrist or other foot care specialist since. Today's visit documents a patient history and a physical examination with visual inspection of the forefoot, hindfoot and toe web spaces, evaluation of protective sensation, foot structure and biomechanics, vascular status and skin integrity, evaluation of the need for special footwear, and patient education. Debridement of plantar calluses and trimming of thickened nails are performed.
cases.note: Boundary: absent sensation at exactly 2 of 5 sites on one foot; last LOPS exam 7 months ago; no interim foot specialist visit.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E11.42) and established diabetic sensory neuropathy with LOPS. Her last foot evaluation for diabetic neuropathy with LOPS, including callus debridement, was 4 months ago, and she has seen no other foot care specialist since. Today's visit documents a patient history and a physical examination with visual inspection of the forefoot, hindfoot and toe web spaces, evaluation of protective sensation, foot structure and biomechanics, vascular status and skin integrity, evaluation of the need for special footwear, and patient education. Corns and calluses are debrided again.
cases.note: Last covered LOPS foot evaluation was only 4 months ago.

Nails are trimmed and debrided.
cases.note: Only 1 of 5 sites absent on each foot: the 2-of-5 threshold must be met on a single foot, not summed.

cases.vignette: 77-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E11.42) and peripheral arterial disease. A superficial blister on the right heel receives local wound care, and corns are debrided.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old man without diabetes (HbA1c 5.3%, normal fasting glucose) who has chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy after oxaliplatin for colon cancer. Testing with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament at five plantar sites per foot, in random order and avoiding callused areas, shows absent sensation at 3 of 5 sites on both feet. He has not had a prior foot evaluation for neuropathy or seen a foot care specialist. Today's visit documents a patient history and a physical examination with visual inspection of the forefoot, hindfoot and toe web spaces, evaluation of protective sensation, foot structure and biomechanics, vascular status and skin integrity, evaluation of the need for special footwear, and patient education. Calluses are debrided.
cases.note: LOPS is from chemotherapy-induced neuropathy in a patient without diabetes; the NCD covers diabetic sensory neuropathy.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E11.42) and diabetic sensory neuropathy with LOPS. Testing with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament at five plantar sites per foot, in random order and avoiding callused areas, shows absent sensation at 3 of 5 sites on the left foot and 2 of 5 on the right. His last foot evaluation for LOPS was 6 months and 3 weeks ago; since then he has seen his endocrinologist twice and his ophthalmologist once, but no podiatrist or other foot care specialist. Nails are trimmed and calluses debrided.
cases.note: Interim visits to an endocrinologist and ophthalmologist are not foot care specialist visits; last LOPS exam 6 months and 3 weeks ago.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E11.42). Testing with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament at five plantar sites per foot, in random order and avoiding callused areas, shows absent sensation at 3 of 5 sites on the left foot. Her last LOPS foot evaluation was 11 months ago and she has seen no foot care specialist since. The visit note documents a history, visual inspection of the forefoot, hindfoot and toe webs, and the sensory testing, then 'calluses debrided'; it does not record any evaluation of foot structure, vascular status or skin integrity, need for special footwear, or patient education.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old woman with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation who started warfarin 4 days ago; her cardiologist plans long-term warfarin therapy. She has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 genotyping. She has enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial comparing genotype-guided warfarin dosing with standard dosing in Medicare-aged adults; its outcomes are major and minor hemorrhage, thromboembolism and mortality. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov by its sponsor before the first subject was enrolled, has a written protocol that addresses the Medicare CED standards, is IRB-approved and complies with 45 CFR Part 46, and specifies public release of results within 24 months of the end of data collection. The test is ordered as part of the trial.
cases.note: Boundary: 4 days of warfarin (fewer than five). Never genotyped; enrolled in a qualifying RCT.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old man with a new proximal deep vein thrombosis, started on warfarin with heparin bridging 5 days ago; he has now completed his fifth day of warfarin in this regimen. He has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 genotyping. He is enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial of genotype-guided versus standard warfarin dosing in Medicare-aged adults, measuring major hemorrhage, minor hemorrhage, recurrent thromboembolism and mortality. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov before the first subject was enrolled, has a written protocol addressing the Medicare CED standards, and is IRB-approved. Genotyping is ordered today as part of the trial.
cases.note: Exactly 5 days of warfarin in the current regimen; the NCD requires fewer than five.

cases.vignette: 77-year-old man with atrial fibrillation who is restarting warfarin after a 2-year break; warfarin was started 2 days ago in this new regimen. During a research study three years ago he had CYP2C9 and VKORC1 genotyping, with results in his chart. He has now enrolled in a different prospective, randomized, controlled trial of genotype-guided warfarin dosing, registered on ClinicalTrials.gov before the first subject was enrolled, with a written protocol addressing the Medicare CED standards and outcomes of hemorrhage, thromboembolism and mortality. The new trial protocol calls for repeat genotyping, and the test is ordered.
cases.note: He was genotyped for CYP2C9 and VKORC1 three years ago; the test is once in a lifetime and the NCD requires no prior testing.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman with a new pulmonary embolism who will start warfarin tomorrow; she has received no warfarin yet. She has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 genotyping. Her hematologist orders CYP2C9 and VKORC1 genotyping through a CLIA-certified laboratory to help choose her starting dose. She is not enrolled in any clinical study, and none is available at her hospital.
cases.note: Not enrolled in any clinical study; outside CED the test is not reasonable and necessary.

cases.vignette: 75-year-old man with atrial fibrillation who started warfarin 2 days ago; he has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 genotyping. He has enrolled in a prospective, single-arm observational registry in which all participants receive genotype-guided dosing and outcomes are compared with historical rates of hemorrhage and thromboembolism; there is no randomization and no concurrent control group. The registry is listed on ClinicalTrials.gov, was registered before the first participant enrolled, and has a written protocol. The genotyping test is ordered as part of the registry.
cases.note: Enrolled in a single-arm observational registry, not a prospective randomized controlled study.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with a left ventricular thrombus who started warfarin 3 days ago; she has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 genotyping. She has enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial comparing genotype-guided with standard warfarin dosing in Medicare-aged adults, measuring major and minor hemorrhage, thromboembolism and mortality. The trial is IRB-approved and has a written protocol that addresses the Medicare CED standards. According to the ClinicalTrials.gov record, the sponsor first registered the trial four months after its first subject was enrolled. The genotyping test is ordered as part of the trial.
cases.note: The RCT was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov four months after the first subject enrolled; registration must precede first enrollment.

cases.vignette: 80-year-old man with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation who took his first dose of warfarin yesterday. Two years ago he took warfarin for 3 months for a provoked calf vein thrombosis, then stopped; he was not genotyped then and has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 testing. He has enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial of genotype-guided versus standard warfarin dosing in Medicare-aged adults that measures major hemorrhage, minor hemorrhage, thromboembolism related to atrial fibrillation, and mortality. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov before the first subject enrolled, has a written protocol addressing the Medicare CED standards, and is IRB-approved. Genotyping is ordered as part of the trial.
cases.note: Distractor: 3 months of warfarin two years ago was a separate regimen; in the current regimen he has had 1 day. Never genotyped.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman (Medicare through disability) with antiphospholipid syndrome and a new venous thromboembolism, for whom warfarin is planned to start after genotyping; she has received no warfarin. Two years ago she had CYP2C19 genotyping before clopidogrel therapy; she has never been tested for CYP2C9 or VKORC1 alleles. She is enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial comparing genotype-guided with standard warfarin dosing in Medicare-aged adults, with outcomes of major hemorrhage, minor hemorrhage, thromboembolism and mortality. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov before the first subject enrolled, has a written protocol that addresses the Medicare CED standards, and is IRB-approved. The CYP2C9/VKORC1 test is ordered as part of the trial.
cases.note: Warfarin not yet started (zero days); never tested; qualifying RCT. Prior genotyping for clopidogrel (CYP2C19) is a distractor, not CYP2C9 or VKORC1.

cases.vignette: 78-year-old woman transferred from an outside hospital with atrial fibrillation, taking warfarin. The transfer medication list shows warfarin 5 mg daily, but the start date is not recorded and the outside hospital's records have not arrived; the patient cannot recall when it was started. She has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 genotyping. She has enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial of genotype-guided versus standard warfarin dosing in Medicare-aged adults, registered on ClinicalTrials.gov before the first subject enrolled, with a written protocol addressing the Medicare CED standards and outcomes of hemorrhage, thromboembolism and mortality. Genotyping is ordered as part of the trial.
cases.note: The start date of the current warfarin regimen is not documented, so it cannot be confirmed that fewer than five days have been given.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with a new deep vein thrombosis who started warfarin 2 days ago; he has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 genotyping. He has enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial at his academic medical center comparing genotype-guided with standard warfarin dosing in Medicare-aged adults, with outcomes of major and minor hemorrhage, thromboembolism and mortality. The study file contains the IRB approval and a written protocol that addresses the Medicare CED standards, but no ClinicalTrials.gov registration number or registration date is recorded in the protocol, the consent form or the order. Genotyping is ordered as part of the trial.
cases.note: The trial is a qualifying RCT in other respects, but its ClinicalTrials.gov registration is not documented anywhere.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old man with newly diagnosed stage IV (metastatic) non-small cell lung adenocarcinoma, with liver and bone metastases. He has decided to pursue systemic cancer treatment. His treating oncologist orders tumor tissue testing with an NGS panel that has FDA approval as a companion in vitro diagnostic with an FDA-approved indication for non-small cell lung cancer. He has never had NGS testing. The test is performed in a CLIA-certified laboratory, which returns results to the oncologist in a report template listing treatment options.
cases.note: Metastatic NSCLC, never NGS tested, seeking chemotherapy/targeted therapy; FDA companion diagnostic indicated for NSCLC; CLIA lab; treating oncologist; report template.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman who underwent resection of a stage II colon adenocarcinoma 3 months ago; surveillance imaging shows no recurrence or metastasis. She wishes to receive any treatment that might help. Her treating oncologist orders tumor NGS testing with an FDA-approved companion diagnostic panel indicated for colorectal cancer, performed in a CLIA-certified laboratory with results returned in a report template listing treatment options. She has never had NGS testing.
cases.note: Stage II colon cancer, resected, with no recurrence: not recurrent, relapsed, refractory, metastatic or stage III/IV.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer whose disease has progressed on her current therapy; she has decided to pursue further treatment. Ten months ago her tumor was tested with an FDA-approved companion diagnostic NGS panel indicated for breast cancer. Her treating oncologist now orders the same NGS panel, for the same genetic content, on the same tumor tissue. The CLIA-certified laboratory would return results in a report template listing treatment options.
cases.note: The same FDA companion diagnostic NGS test was already run on the same cancer 10 months ago; repeat for the same genetic content is not covered.

cases.vignette: 78-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who has decided against any further cancer treatment and enrolled in hospice. His daughter asks whether tumor testing could provide information for the family, and his oncologist orders tumor NGS testing with an FDA-approved companion diagnostic panel indicated for pancreatic cancer, in a CLIA-certified laboratory with a report template listing treatment options. He has never had NGS testing.
cases.note: Patient has chosen hospice and declined further cancer treatment.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman with stage IIIC cutaneous melanoma who has decided to pursue systemic therapy. At diagnosis, a single-gene BRAF test using real-time PCR (not NGS) was performed. Her treating oncologist now orders tumor testing with an NGS panel that has FDA approval as a companion in vitro diagnostic with an FDA-approved indication for melanoma. She has never had NGS testing. The test is performed in a CLIA-certified laboratory, which reports to the oncologist in a template that lists treatment options.
cases.note: Advanced stage III melanoma; a prior single-gene PCR test is a distractor because it was not the same NGS test.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old man with lung adenocarcinoma confirmed on biopsy 1 week ago. Staging imaging has been ordered but not yet performed, and no stage, nodal status or metastatic status is documented anywhere in the record. He has decided to pursue cancer treatment. His treating oncologist orders tumor NGS testing with an FDA-approved companion diagnostic panel indicated for non-small cell lung cancer, in a CLIA-certified laboratory with a report template listing treatment options. He has never had NGS testing.
cases.note: Lung adenocarcinoma with staging pending; the record does not show recurrent, metastatic or stage III/IV disease, and nothing shows earlier-stage disease.

cases.vignette: 58-year-old woman with breast cancer diagnosed this year. Her sister was diagnosed with ovarian cancer at age 48. Her treating oncologist documents that this family history is a risk factor for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer and that she has a clinical indication for germline testing. The oncologist orders an FDA-approved germline NGS hereditary cancer panel. She has never had germline testing. The test is performed in a CLIA-certified laboratory, which returns results to the oncologist in a report template listing treatment options.
cases.note: Germline NGS in breast cancer with a documented clinical indication and risk factor, never previously tested; FDA-approved test, CLIA lab, report template.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with recurrent high-grade serous ovarian cancer. At her original diagnosis 3 years ago she had germline testing with an FDA-approved germline NGS hereditary cancer panel, which found no pathogenic variants. Her treating oncologist documents a clinical indication and a risk factor (Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry) for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer, and orders the same germline NGS panel, for the same genetic content, again in a CLIA-certified laboratory with a report template listing treatment options.
cases.note: Germline: the same germline NGS panel for the same content was performed 3 years ago.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with newly diagnosed breast cancer. Her treating oncologist's note states 'clinical indication for germline testing' and orders an FDA-approved germline NGS hereditary cancer panel, to be run in a CLIA-certified laboratory that reports in a template listing treatment options. She has never had germline testing. The note's family history section reads 'not obtained,' and the record contains no other information about family history, ancestry, age at diagnosis, tumor features or any other risk factor for inherited breast or ovarian cancer.
cases.note: Germline: breast cancer with a documented clinical indication, but no risk factor is documented and the family history was not taken; nothing shows absence of risk factors.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old man with metastatic colorectal cancer who has decided to pursue further chemotherapy. He has never had NGS testing. His treating oncologist sends tumor tissue for an NGS panel that has FDA approval as a companion diagnostic with an FDA-approved indication for colorectal cancer. However, the sample is sequenced at a university research laboratory that is not CLIA-certified; results would be returned to the oncologist in a report template listing treatment options.
cases.note: All patient criteria are met, but the test is run in a research laboratory that is not CLIA-certified (required by both sections B and D).

cases.vignette: 58-year-old woman with class II obesity, BMI 35.0 kg/m2 (height 165 cm, weight 95.3 kg), and type 2 diabetes mellitus (ICD-10-CM E11.9) with HbA1c 8.4% on metformin and insulin. She completed a 6-month physician-supervised weight management program with dietitian counseling and a trial of anti-obesity medication, losing only 2% of body weight and regaining it. Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is requested.
cases.note: Boundary: BMI exactly 35.0 meets >= 35; type 2 diabetes is a qualifying co-morbidity.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with BMI 48.2 kg/m2 (ICD-10-CM E66.01, Z68.41) and severe obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP. Over the past 2 years he failed a medically supervised low-calorie diet program and 9 months of a GLP-1 receptor agonist with minimal sustained weight loss. Open biliopancreatic diversion with duodenal switch is requested at a community hospital whose bariatric program is not certified by the American College of Surgeons or the American Society for Bariatric Surgery.
cases.note: Open BPD/DS, BMI 48, OSA; lack of Center of Excellence certification is irrelevant (not required since Sept 24, 2013).

cases.vignette: 61-year-old woman with BMI 34.6 kg/m2 and type 2 diabetes mellitus (ICD-10-CM E11.65) with HbA1c 9.1% and hypertension. She completed a 6-month physician-supervised weight management program with dietitian counseling and a trial of anti-obesity medication, losing only 2% of body weight and regaining it. Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is requested.
cases.note: BMI 34.6 is below 35, despite qualifying diabetes and failed medical therapy.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with BMI 41.3 kg/m2 (ICD-10-CM E66.01, Z68.41). She has normal blood pressure, normal fasting glucose and HbA1c, no sleep apnea on a sleep study, normal lipids and no joint disease, and takes no medications. She completed a 6-month physician-supervised weight management program with dietitian counseling and a trial of anti-obesity medication, losing only 2% of body weight and regaining it. Laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding is requested to treat her obesity.
cases.note: BMI 41 but no obesity-related co-morbidity: treatment of obesity alone.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with BMI 43 kg/m2, type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Over 1 year he failed a supervised diet and exercise program and anti-obesity medication. Because of extensive adhesions from prior abdominal surgery, his surgeon requests an open (not laparoscopic) adjustable gastric band placement.
cases.note: Open adjustable gastric banding is non-covered for all beneficiaries.

cases.vignette: 59-year-old woman with BMI 38 kg/m2 and obstructive sleep apnea, who has failed a supervised dietary program and anti-obesity medication. She prefers to avoid surgery, and her physician requests endoscopic placement of an intragastric balloon for weight loss.
cases.note: Gastric balloon for obesity is non-covered.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old man with BMI 46 kg/m2, type 2 diabetes and hypertension, who has failed a 6-month medically supervised weight-loss program. Because of a large ventral hernia requiring concurrent repair, his surgeon requests an open sleeve gastrectomy.
cases.note: Open sleeve gastrectomy is non-covered for all beneficiaries.

cases.vignette: 60-year-old woman with BMI 39.4 kg/m2 and hypertension (ICD-10-CM I10) treated with two agents. She completed a 6-month physician-supervised weight management program with dietitian counseling and a trial of anti-obesity medication, losing only 2% of body weight and regaining it. Laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding is requested.
cases.note: LAGB, BMI 39, hypertension, failed medical therapy.

cases.vignette: 63-year-old man with BMI 40.5 kg/m2 and hypertension and type 2 diabetes. The surgical referral note documents his weight, BMI and co-morbidities and requests laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. The record contains no information about any prior diet program, supervised weight management, medication or other medical treatment for obesity, or its outcome.
cases.note: BMI and co-morbidity documented, but no record of any prior medical treatment for obesity.

cases.vignette: 57-year-old woman with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (ICD-10-CM E11.9) and osteoarthritis of both knees. Her weight is recorded as 98 kg; no height, BMI or other measure of adiposity appears anywhere in the record. She completed a 6-month physician-supervised weight management program with dietitian counseling and a trial of anti-obesity medication, losing only 2% of body weight and regaining it. Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is requested.
cases.note: Weight documented without height or BMI, so BMI >= 35 cannot be confirmed.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, ICD-10-CM C84.00), stage IIB, with widespread patches, plaques and two tumors on the trunk and thighs. Over the past 3 years his skin disease did not respond to high-potency topical corticosteroids, narrowband UVB phototherapy, or 6 months of oral bexarotene. His dermatologist requests extracorporeal photopheresis as palliative treatment of the skin lesions and pruritus.
cases.note: CTCL skin disease that failed several prior therapies; ECP is palliative.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with Sézary syndrome (ICD-10-CM C84.10) diagnosed 2 weeks ago with erythroderma, intense pruritus and circulating Sézary cells. She has received no treatment of any kind for the lymphoma. Her dermatologist requests extracorporeal photopheresis as the initial (first) treatment for her skin manifestations because of its favorable side-effect profile.
cases.note: Newly diagnosed CTCL with no prior therapy: coverage requires disease that has not responded to other therapy.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man 4 months after orthotopic heart transplantation, maintained on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone. Endomyocardial biopsy shows acute cellular rejection grade 2R. He received 3 days of pulse intravenous methylprednisolone, then a 7-day course of antithymocyte globulin; repeat biopsy still shows grade 2R rejection with new mild LV dysfunction. His transplant cardiologist requests extracorporeal photopheresis.
cases.note: Acute cardiac allograft rejection that persisted despite pulse steroids and antithymocyte globulin.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman 6 weeks after heart transplantation on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone. A routine surveillance biopsy yesterday shows acute cellular rejection grade 2R, her first rejection episode. No augmented immunosuppression has been given yet. Her team requests extracorporeal photopheresis to begin this week as the initial treatment of the rejection, in place of pulse corticosteroids.
cases.note: First episode of acute cardiac rejection, no standard treatment tried yet: not refractory.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man 5 months after deceased-donor kidney transplantation with biopsy-proven acute cellular rejection. The rejection did not respond to pulse methylprednisolone or a full course of antithymocyte globulin, and creatinine continues to rise. His nephrologist requests extracorporeal photopheresis for the steroid- and antibody-refractory renal allograft rejection.
cases.note: Refractory acute rejection of a kidney (not cardiac) allograft is not a covered indication.

cases.vignette: 65-year-old woman 14 months after allogeneic stem cell transplantation for AML, now with chronic graft-versus-host disease (ICD-10-CM D89.811) involving skin sclerosis, oral lichenoid changes and ocular dryness. Her disease progressed despite 3 months of prednisone 1 mg/kg combined with tacrolimus, and did not improve after adding sirolimus. Her transplant physician requests extracorporeal photopheresis.
cases.note: Chronic GVHD refractory to steroids and a calcineurin inhibitor.

cases.vignette: 63-year-old man 35 days after allogeneic stem cell transplantation with acute graft-versus-host disease (ICD-10-CM D89.810) grade III of skin and gut. He has not responded to 7 days of methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg/day plus tacrolimus. There are no features of chronic GVHD. His transplant physician requests extracorporeal photopheresis for steroid-refractory acute GVHD.
cases.note: Steroid-refractory ACUTE GVHD: only chronic GVHD is covered.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old woman 2 years after allogeneic stem cell transplantation for myelodysplastic syndrome, referred with chronic graft-versus-host disease (ICD-10-CM D89.811) of the skin and mouth. The referral consists of a one-page consult note describing the skin and oral findings and requesting extracorporeal photopheresis. The note does not state what immunosuppressive treatment, if any, she has received for GVHD, or how the disease responded; no medication list or prior treatment records are included.
cases.note: Chronic GVHD, but nothing documents what immunosuppression has been tried or that the disease is refractory.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with ileocolonic Crohn's disease (ICD-10-CM K50.80) refractory to corticosteroids, azathioprine, infliximab, vedolizumab and ustekinumab. Surgery has been declined. His gastroenterologist requests extracorporeal photopheresis as an immunomodulatory therapy.
cases.note: Refractory Crohn's disease is not a listed indication; all other indications are non-covered.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old man with mycosis fungoides (ICD-10-CM C84.00) with plaques covering about 30% of his body surface area, referred by an outside dermatologist. The request for extracorporeal photopheresis as palliative treatment of the skin lesions states 'prior therapies per outside records'; those records were not received, and the submitted documentation contains only the biopsy report and photographs of the lesions.
cases.note: CTCL skin disease, but there is no record of prior therapy or response, so 'not responded to other therapy' cannot be confirmed.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive acquired myasthenia gravis (ICD-10-CM G70.01) with worsening bulbar weakness and dysphagia over 2 weeks despite pyridostigmine and prednisone. A course of five plasma exchange sessions is requested in the hospital outpatient apheresis unit before starting a steroid-sparing agent.
cases.note: Plasma exchange for acquired myasthenia gravis in a hospital outpatient department.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with Guillain-Barre syndrome (ICD-10-CM G61.0) diagnosed 4 days ago by clinical findings, CSF albuminocytologic dissociation and nerve conduction studies. He has distal weakness and areflexia but can still walk 10 meters unaided and has normal respiratory function. Plasma exchange as an inpatient is requested.
cases.note: Guillain-Barre syndrome is listed without a severity or last-resort qualifier; mild, ambulatory disease is a distractor.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old woman with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (chronic relapsing polyneuropathy, ICD-10-CM G61.81) now unable to walk without a walker, with severe proximal and distal weakness. She failed to respond to 6 months of IVIG and to high-dose oral prednisone. Plasma exchange in the hospital outpatient department is requested.
cases.note: Severe chronic relapsing polyneuropathy (CIDP) that failed IVIG and steroids.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with chronic relapsing polyneuropathy (CIDP, ICD-10-CM G61.81) with mild distal paresthesias and minimal foot weakness; he walks normally, works full time and has no respiratory or bulbar involvement. His symptoms did not improve after 3 months of IVIG. Plasma exchange in the hospital outpatient department is requested.
cases.note: CIDP with mild symptoms: requires severe or life-threatening symptoms (and failed conventional therapy).

cases.vignette: 76-year-old man with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (ICD-10-CM C88.0) with IgM 6,200 mg/dL, headaches, blurred vision and retinal venous engorgement from hyperviscosity. Plasmapheresis is requested at a freestanding physician-directed apheresis clinic where a physician is on site to perform medical services and respond to emergencies at all times during patient care hours, each patient is under a physician's care, and the apheresis nurses work under the direct, personal supervision of the on-site physician.
cases.note: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia in a physician-directed clinic meeting all nonhospital-setting conditions.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old woman with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (ICD-10-CM G70.01) with worsening generalized weakness despite pyridostigmine and azathioprine. Maintenance plasma exchange is requested at a freestanding infusion and apheresis clinic. Her neurologist oversees her care, but the sessions are run by apheresis nurses, and no physician is on site during clinic hours; the medical director is available by telephone and comes in once a week.
cases.note: Nonhospital clinic with no physician present during patient care hours (available by phone only).

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus (ICD-10-CM M32.9) with photosensitive rash and inflammatory arthritis of the hands. Kidney function, urinalysis, blood counts and neurologic and cardiopulmonary findings are normal. Her rash and joint pain persisted despite hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone. Plasmapheresis in the hospital outpatient department is requested.
cases.note: SLE with non-life-threatening manifestations (rash, arthritis): not last-resort treatment of life-threatening SLE.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old man with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis who developed rheumatoid vasculitis (ICD-10-CM M05.20) with mononeuritis multiplex and mesenteric ischemia, considered life-threatening. He was admitted yesterday and has not yet received any treatment for the vasculitis; the rheumatologist requests plasma exchange to begin today as first-line therapy, with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide to be considered later if needed.
cases.note: Life-threatening rheumatoid vasculitis, but plasma exchange is requested as initial therapy, not as last resort.

cases.vignette: 65-year-old woman with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (ICD-10-CM M34.1) with skin thickening of the fingers and Raynaud phenomenon. Pulmonary function, echocardiogram, kidney function and blood pressure are normal, with no digital ulcers. Her skin thickening progressed despite 12 months of methotrexate. Plasmapheresis in the hospital outpatient department is requested.
cases.note: Scleroderma limited to skin and not life-threatening.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old man with biopsy-proven polymyositis (ICD-10-CM M33.20) with severe proximal weakness, dysphagia with aspiration and early respiratory muscle weakness, admitted to the ICU. His rheumatologist requests inpatient plasma exchange. The admission note describes his current status but does not state what treatment, if any, he has received for polymyositis or how he responded, and no medication history is included.
cases.note: Life-threatening polymyositis, but no record of conventional therapy or response.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old woman with cryoglobulinemia (ICD-10-CM D89.1) causing purpura and progressive neuropathy. Plasmapheresis is requested at a freestanding physician-directed clinic. The clinic's attestation states that a physician is present on site at all times during patient care hours and that each patient is under a physician's care; it says nothing about who performs the apheresis or how the technicians and nurses are supervised, and no other description of the clinic's staffing is provided.
cases.note: Nonhospital clinic: physician presence documented, but nothing shows nonphysician services are under direct, personal physician supervision.

cases.vignette: Request date is the reference point. 69-year-old woman with myelodysplastic syndrome (ICD-10-CM D46.9) diagnosed 5 months ago with transfusion-dependent anemia and thrombocytopenia. Bone marrow biopsy 3 weeks ago: 7% blasts with intermediate-risk cytogenetics. Her IPSS-R score, calculated and documented by the hematologist, is 4.5 (high risk). No HLA-matched sibling or unrelated adult donor was found, so an allogeneic transplant using umbilical cord blood stem cell products is planned after reduced-intensity conditioning. Cardiac, pulmonary, renal and hepatic testing show adequate organ function. The transplant center is experienced in cord blood transplantation.
cases.note: Boundary: IPSS-R exactly 4.5 meets the >= 4.5 threshold; cord blood is an allowed stem cell source.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00), International Staging System (ISS) Stage II at diagnosis 14 months ago, high-risk cytogenetics, in very good partial response after induction and a prior autologous transplant. An allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant from an HLA-matched unrelated donor is requested. He has signed informed consent and is enrolled in a prospective clinical study of allogeneic HSCT for multiple myeloma that appears on the CMS list of approved Coverage with Evidence Development studies; the study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, its protocol addresses graft-versus-host disease, transplant-related adverse events and overall survival, and its analysis plan adjusts for age, ISS stage, conditioning regimen, donor type and cell source.
cases.note: Allogeneic HSCT for ISS stage II myeloma inside a CMS-approved CED study: both C3 and C4 met.

cases.vignette: 61-year-old woman with Durie-Salmon Stage III multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) who relapsed 10 months after an autologous transplant and is now in partial response after salvage therapy. An allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant from her HLA-identical brother is requested. Organ function is adequate and she has an excellent performance status. The transplant center does not participate in any clinical study of allogeneic transplant for myeloma; the transplant will be performed as standard care, and she is not enrolled in any study or registry.
cases.note: Allogeneic HSCT for myeloma is covered only within an approved prospective study; this patient is treated off-study.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with primary myelofibrosis (ICD-10-CM D47.1) diagnosed 2 years ago, with splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms partly controlled on ruxolitinib. His hematologist documents a DIPSSplus risk category of Intermediate-1. He is enrolled, with signed informed consent, in a CMS-approved prospective clinical study of allogeneic HSCT for myelofibrosis registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. An allogeneic transplant from a matched unrelated donor is requested.
cases.note: DIPSSplus Intermediate-1 does not meet the Intermediate-2 or High requirement, even inside an approved study.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with post-polycythemia vera (secondary) myelofibrosis (ICD-10-CM D47.1) with progressive anemia and a spleen 14 cm below the costal margin. She is enrolled, with signed informed consent, in a CMS-approved prospective clinical study of allogeneic HSCT for myelofibrosis registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. An allogeneic transplant from an HLA-matched sibling is requested. The referral packet contains the bone marrow pathology report and donor typing; no DIPSS, DIPSSplus or other prognostic risk score is recorded anywhere in the record.
cases.note: Patient is in an approved MF study, but no DIPSSplus risk category is documented, so eligibility cannot be confirmed.

cases.vignette: 78-year-old man with biopsy-proven primary (AL) amyloid light chain amyloidosis (ICD-10-CM E85.81) with lambda light chains, with amyloid involvement of the kidneys (nephrotic-range proteinuria) and heart; no liver, nerve or gastrointestinal involvement on evaluation. Echocardiogram 2 weeks ago shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%. The team selected him using recognized clinical risk factors (troponin, NT-proBNP, performance status). High-dose melphalan followed by autologous stem cell transplantation is requested.
cases.note: Primary AL amyloidosis, 2 organs, EF 55%. Age 78 is a distractor: the age >= 64 exclusion applied only through March 14, 2005.

cases.vignette: 63-year-old woman with primary (AL) amyloid light chain amyloidosis (ICD-10-CM E85.81) confirmed on fat pad and renal biopsy, with amyloid involvement limited to the kidneys and heart. Recognized clinical risk factors were used to select her for transplant. Echocardiogram 1 week ago reports a left ventricular ejection fraction of 45%; a cardiac MRI the same week also measured 45%. Renal function is moderately reduced and she is fully ambulatory. High-dose melphalan with autologous stem cell transplantation is requested.
cases.note: Boundary miss: LVEF exactly 45% is not greater than 45%.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old man with Durie-Salmon Stage III multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) who received a first autologous stem cell transplant 3 months ago after induction (very good partial response, paraprotein down 92%, sustained). Cardiac, renal, pulmonary and hepatic function are adequate. Per the transplant center's planned protocol, a second autologous stem cell transplant (the second of two planned sequential rounds) is now requested to deepen the response.
cases.note: Second planned AuSCT for myeloma is tandem transplantation, which is non-covered.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman with Durie-Salmon Stage III IgG kappa multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) diagnosed 6 months ago. After four cycles of induction chemotherapy her serum M-protein fell from 4.0 to 1.8 g/dL (a 55% decrease), and the reduction has been sustained on repeat testing for 6 weeks. Pre-transplant evaluation documents LVEF 60%, creatinine clearance 65 mL/min, DLCO 78% predicted and normal liver function tests. She has not had a prior transplant. A single autologous stem cell transplant after high-dose melphalan is requested.
cases.note: Single AuSCT, Durie-Salmon stage III, partial response (55% paraprotein drop sustained 6 weeks), adequate organ function documented.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old man with IgA multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) staged as Durie-Salmon Stage I (hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, normal calcium, a single small lytic lesion, low M-protein). He is newly diagnosed and responded to induction chemotherapy with a 70% decrease in serum paraprotein sustained for 2 months. Cardiac, renal, pulmonary and hepatic function are all adequate. A single autologous stem cell transplant is requested.
cases.note: Durie-Salmon stage I: single AuSCT for myeloma is covered only for stage II or III.

cases.vignette: 65-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia (ICD-10-CM C92.00) that is primary refractory: after two induction courses, day-28 bone marrow shows 30% blasts. She has no HLA-matched sibling or unrelated donor. Organ function is adequate. Her physician requests high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplantation using stem cells collected earlier.
cases.note: AuSCT for acute leukemia not in remission is explicitly non-covered.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with Durie-Salmon Stage II multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) diagnosed 5 months ago. After induction his urine and serum paraprotein fell by 65%, sustained for 2 months on repeat testing. This would be his first transplant; a single autologous stem cell transplant is requested. The submitted record contains the staging workup, the response labs and the induction treatment notes, but no echocardiogram, pulmonary function testing, renal function or liver function results and no statement about organ function.
cases.note: Stage II, responsive myeloma, single AuSCT, but no assessment of cardiac, renal, pulmonary or hepatic function is in the record.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with relapsed metastatic nonseminomatous germ cell tumor of the testis (ICD-10-CM C62.91) that recurred after first-line cisplatin-based chemotherapy. His oncologist requests high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell rescue. Organ function is adequate and stem cells have been collected.
cases.note: AuSCT for a solid tumor other than neuroblastoma (germ cell tumor) is non-covered.

cases.vignette: 61-year-old man with a closed left tibial shaft fracture treated in a long-leg cast 8 months ago, now coded ICD-10-CM S82.202K (nonunion). Radiograph sets (AP, lateral, and both obliques) were taken at 4.5 months and again at 8 months after injury, 105 days apart; the radiologist reports no interval change and no bridging callus, i.e., healing has ceased for more than 3 months. The orthopedist orders a noninvasive electrical osteogenic stimulator worn over the cast site.
cases.note: Tibial nonunion at 8 months; two multi-view radiograph sets 105 days apart show no healing.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old woman with a scaphoid waist fracture of the right wrist sustained 7 months ago and treated in a thumb spica cast; she has had no surgery. Two radiograph sets of the wrist, each with PA, lateral, oblique, and scaphoid views, were obtained exactly 90 days apart before any stimulator treatment. The radiologist's written interpretation states there has been no clinically significant evidence of fracture healing between the two sets. The hand surgeon orders a low-intensity pulsed ultrasonic osteogenic stimulator. She is not using any other bone-growth stimulator.
cases.note: Ultrasonic for scaphoid nonunion: ultrasonic coverage is not limited to long bones, and since 2005 no prior surgery is needed. Radiograph sets exactly 90 days apart.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old man with a right femoral shaft fracture treated with an intramedullary nail 4 months ago. Radiograph sets with AP and lateral views were taken at 2 weeks and at 4 months after surgery, 95 days apart, and show minimal callus with no progression between them. The orthopedist, concerned about slow healing because the patient smokes, orders a noninvasive electrical osteogenic stimulator now.
cases.note: Only 4 months since fracture; electrical stimulator nonunion requires >= 6 months.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with a humeral shaft fracture treated in a functional brace 9 months ago. The fracture remains clinically mobile and painful. Two radiograph sets of the humerus, each with AP and lateral views, were taken at 7 months and at 9 months after injury, 60 days apart, and show no healing. No other radiographs exist. Her orthopedist orders a noninvasive electrical osteogenic stimulator.
cases.note: Fracture 9 months old, but the two radiograph sets are only 60 days apart.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with degenerative spondylolisthesis and stenosis scheduled for an instrumented posterolateral fusion from L3 to L5 (three vertebrae: L3, L4, L5). He has had no previous spinal surgery. The spine surgeon orders a noninvasive electrical osteogenic stimulator as an adjunct to the fusion, to begin after surgery.
cases.note: Boundary: L3-L5 involves exactly 3 vertebrae, which qualifies as multiple level fusion.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes who smokes one pack per day, scheduled for her first spinal fusion: a single-level instrumented fusion at L4-L5 (two vertebrae). The surgeon documents that her smoking and diabetes put her at high risk of pseudarthrosis and orders a noninvasive electrical osteogenic stimulator as an adjunct to the fusion surgery.
cases.note: Single-level L4-L5 fusion (2 vertebrae) and no prior failed fusion. Smoking and diabetes are not NCD criteria.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old man who underwent an L5-S1 fusion exactly 9 months ago; that was his last surgery. CT shows no bridging bone across the fusion level and the surgeon diagnoses a failed fusion (pseudarthrosis). The surgeon orders a noninvasive electrical osteogenic stimulator to treat the failed fusion.
cases.note: Boundary: failed fusion exactly 9 months after the last surgery (noninvasive electrical).

cases.vignette: 74-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer who sustained a pathologic fracture of the left femoral shaft through a lytic metastasis 10 months ago. Two radiograph sets with multiple views, obtained 120 days apart before any stimulator treatment, carry a radiologist's written interpretation of no clinically significant healing between them. Her oncologist and orthopedist order an ultrasonic osteogenic stimulator for the nonunion.
cases.note: Tumor-related nonunion (pathologic fracture through metastasis) is excluded, despite proper radiographs.

cases.vignette: 41-year-old man on Medicare through disability with congenital pseudarthrosis of the right tibia (ICD-10-CM Q74.2), with persistent motion at the pseudarthrosis site on radiographs. His orthopedic surgeon plans to implant an invasive (implantable) electrical osteogenic stimulator with a coiled cathode at the pseudarthrosis site during the same operation as a bone graft.
cases.note: Congenital pseudarthrosis is covered only for the noninvasive device; an invasive stimulator is requested.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman with a distal radius shaft fracture 8 months ago treated in a cast. Two radiograph sets of the forearm, each with AP, lateral, and oblique views, were obtained 100 days apart before treatment; the image files are attached to the order. The record contains no written interpretation of either set by any physician. The orthopedist orders an ultrasonic osteogenic stimulator; she uses no other bone-growth device.
cases.note: Two radiograph sets 100 days apart exist, but no physician written interpretation is in the record.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old man with a left tibial shaft fracture 10 months ago, treated with a cast and then a fracture brace; he has persistent pain and motion at the fracture site. The order for a noninvasive electrical osteogenic stimulator is accompanied by one radiograph set taken last week (AP, lateral, two obliques) showing a persistent fracture line. No other radiographs are in the record.
cases.note: Fracture 10 months old but the record contains only one radiograph set; serial radiographs not documented.

cases.vignette: 65-year-old man with a tibial shaft nonunion 9 months after injury. Two multi-view radiograph sets taken 110 days apart before treatment have a radiologist's written interpretation of no clinically significant healing between them. He has been using a noninvasive electrical osteogenic stimulator for 6 weeks and will continue it. His surgeon also orders an ultrasonic osteogenic stimulator to be used daily at the same time to speed healing.
cases.note: Ultrasonic stimulator would be used concurrently with a noninvasive electrical stimulator.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with chronic intractable lumbar radicular pain for 4 years after two lumbar decompressions (ICD-10-CM M96.1). He has tried gabapentin, duloxetine, and opioids without satisfactory relief, 12 weeks of physical therapy, epidural steroid injections, and cognitive behavioral therapy; the spine surgeon judges further surgery unsuitable. Before implantation he was evaluated by a multidisciplinary pain team, including a physical evaluation by a pain physician and a psychological evaluation by a pain psychologist, who cleared him. A 7-day trial with temporarily implanted percutaneous epidural electrodes reduced his leg pain from 8/10 to 3/10 and improved walking. The implanting center has the facilities, equipment, and staff for diagnosis, device training, programming, and follow-up. Request: permanent percutaneous epidural spinal cord stimulator implantation.
cases.note: All five conditions met for a percutaneous epidural spinal cord stimulator.

cases.vignette: 58-year-old woman on Medicare through disability with complex regional pain syndrome of the right leg for 3 years and chronic intractable pain. She tried gabapentin, nortriptyline, and topical agents without relief, completed graded motor imagery and physical therapy, and had psychological pain management. Her physicians judge opioids contraindicated because of a prior opioid use disorder, now in sustained remission for 6 years, and there is no surgical treatment for her condition. A multidisciplinary team performed physical and psychological evaluations before implantation and recommended neurostimulation. A 5-day trial with a temporarily implanted epidural electrode reduced pain from 9/10 to 4/10. The center has full facilities and staff for training and follow-up. Request: permanent dorsal column stimulator implantation.
cases.note: Opioids judged contraindicated (prior opioid use disorder) and surgery unsuitable, which the NCD accepts; the history is a distractor.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old man with chronic intractable neuropathic leg pain after lumbar surgery 3 years ago. Medications, physical therapy, cognitive therapy, and a repeat surgical opinion (no further surgery recommended) have not provided satisfactory relief. A multidisciplinary team completed physical and psychological evaluations. The implanting center has the necessary facilities and staff. Because he had excellent short-term relief from two epidural steroid injections, the surgeon plans to proceed directly to a permanent spinal cord stimulator implant without a temporary electrode trial, to spare him a second procedure.
cases.note: No temporary electrode trial; good relief from steroid injections does not substitute.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with chronic intractable low back and leg pain for 5 years after a lumbar fusion. Medications including opioids, physical therapy, and psychological counseling did not prove satisfactory, and her surgeon judges further surgery unsuitable.
