He has no history of injection drug use and has never received a blood transfusion. He has never been screened for hepatitis C. The physician orders an FDA-approved HCV antibody test, performed per its labeling by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Boundary: born December 1965, inside the 1945-1965 cohort; never screened; no risk factors needed.

cases.vignette: 60-year-old woman (Medicare through disability) born in January 1966, seen by her general internist at her primary care practice. She has several tattoos obtained at licensed parlors and used intranasal cocaine in her twenties. She has never injected drugs and has never received a blood transfusion. She has never been screened for hepatitis C. The internist orders an FDA-approved HCV antibody screening test, run by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Born January 1966, just outside the birth cohort; tattoos and past intranasal cocaine use are not high-risk factors under this NCD.

cases.vignette: 55-year-old man (Medicare through disability) born in 1970, seen by his nurse practitioner at his primary care clinic. His history, documented at this visit, includes multiple blood transfusions after a motor vehicle accident in 1988. He has never injected drugs and has never been screened for hepatitis C. The nurse practitioner documents that he is at high risk and orders an FDA-approved HCV antibody test, performed by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Born 1970 (outside the cohort) but high risk: blood transfusion in 1988, before 1992.

cases.vignette: 50-year-old woman (Medicare through disability) born in 1975, seen by her family physician at her primary care practice. She received a blood transfusion in March 1992 after childbirth. She has never injected drugs and has never been screened for hepatitis C. The physician documents the transfusion history and orders an FDA-approved HCV antibody screening test, run by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Boundary: transfusion in March 1992 is not 'prior to 1992'; born 1975, so neither high risk nor in the birth cohort.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man born in 1953, seen by his general internist at his primary care practice for an annual wellness visit. He had a negative Medicare-covered HCV antibody screening test 4 years ago. He has never injected drugs and has never received a blood transfusion, and he reports no new exposures. The internist orders a repeat FDA-approved HCV antibody screening test, run by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Birth-cohort screening is a single test; he already had a negative screening test 4 years ago and has no high-risk factors.

cases.vignette: 44-year-old man (Medicare through disability) seen by his family physician at his primary care clinic. He had a negative HCV antibody screening test 14 months ago. He reports that he has continued to inject heroin regularly since that test, and the physician documents ongoing illicit injection drug use. The physician orders a repeat FDA-approved HCV antibody screening test, performed by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: High risk with continued illicit injection drug use since the prior negative screen 14 months ago: annual repeat is covered.

cases.vignette: 47-year-old woman (Medicare through disability) born in 1978, seen by her nurse practitioner at her primary care practice. She injected drugs in her twenties but stopped 10 years ago and has been abstinent since, confirmed at each visit. She had a negative HCV antibody screening test 2 years ago. She has never received a blood transfusion. The nurse practitioner orders a repeat FDA-approved HCV antibody screening test, run by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Past injection drug use stopped 10 years ago; no injection drug use since the prior negative screen 2 years ago, so repeat screening is not covered.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man born in 1958, seen in a hospital emergency department for an ankle sprain. He has never injected drugs, never received a blood transfusion, and has never been screened for hepatitis C. The emergency physician orders an FDA-approved HCV antibody screening test during the visit as part of the department's opportunistic screening program, run by the hospital's CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Ordered by an emergency physician in the emergency department, which is not a primary care setting, even though the patient is in the birth cohort.

cases.vignette: 51-year-old man (Medicare through disability) born in 1974, seen by his family physician at his primary care practice. His problem list documents a history of illicit injection drug use. He had a negative HCV antibody screening test 18 months ago. The note does not document whether he has injected drugs at any time since that test; the substance-use section is blank. The physician orders a repeat FDA-approved HCV antibody screening test, run by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Repeat screen for a person with past injection drug use, but the record does not say whether injection drug use has continued since the prior negative test.

cases.vignette: 45-year-old woman (Medicare through disability) born in 1980, seen by her general internist at her primary care practice. She has never injected drugs. She reports receiving a blood transfusion during surgery 'as a child or teenager' but does not know the year, and no records of the surgery are available. She has never been screened for hepatitis C. The internist orders an FDA-approved HCV antibody screening test, run by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
cases.note: Born 1980, so outside the cohort; she reports a transfusion in childhood or adolescence but the year (before or after 1992) is not documented.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old woman, current smoker, 1 pack/day for 35 years. No cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or other respiratory symptoms. Requesting her first LDCT screening. A counseling and shared decision-making visit was documented 2 weeks ago: eligibility was confirmed, a decision aid was used, adherence to annual screening and comorbidities were discussed, and smoking cessation counseling was provided. Order on file from the primary care physician for lung cancer screening with LDCT. Reading radiologist is ABR board-certified. The imaging center reports nodules using Lung-RADS.
cases.note: Typical eligible beneficiary.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old man who smoked 40 cigarettes a day for 10 years and quit 14 years ago. Asymptomatic. First LDCT screening requested. A counseling and shared decision-making visit was documented 2 weeks ago: eligibility was confirmed, a decision aid was used, adherence to annual screening and comorbidities were discussed, and smoking cessation counseling was provided. Order on file from the primary care physician for lung cancer screening with LDCT. Reading radiologist is ABR board-certified. The imaging center reports nodules using Lung-RADS.
cases.note: Boundary: 2 packs/day x 10 years = exactly 20 pack-years; quit 14 years ago (within 15).

cases.vignette: 79-year-old man, former smoker of 1 pack/day for 40 years, quit 5 years ago. Asymptomatic. First LDCT screening requested. A counseling and shared decision-making visit was documented 2 weeks ago: eligibility was confirmed, a decision aid was used, adherence to annual screening and comorbidities were discussed, and smoking cessation counseling was provided. Order on file from the primary care physician for lung cancer screening with LDCT. Reading radiologist is ABR board-certified. The imaging center reports nodules using Lung-RADS.
cases.note: Age 79 exceeds the 50-77 range.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman, 30 pack-year history, quit smoking 18 years ago. Asymptomatic. First LDCT screening requested. A counseling and shared decision-making visit was documented 2 weeks ago: eligibility was confirmed, a decision aid was used, adherence to annual screening and comorbidities were discussed, and smoking cessation counseling was provided. Order on file from the primary care physician for lung cancer screening with LDCT. Reading radiologist is ABR board-certified. The imaging center reports nodules using Lung-RADS.
cases.note: Quit 18 years ago, outside the 15-year window.

cases.vignette: 58-year-old man, current smoker of 30 cigarettes a day for the past 10 years; never smoked before that. Asymptomatic. First LDCT screening requested. A counseling and shared decision-making visit was documented 2 weeks ago: eligibility was confirmed, a decision aid was used, adherence to annual screening and comorbidities were discussed, and smoking cessation counseling was provided. Order on file from the primary care physician for lung cancer screening with LDCT. Reading radiologist is ABR board-certified. The imaging center reports nodules using Lung-RADS.
cases.note: 1.5 packs/day x 10 years = 15 pack-years, below 20.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man, current smoker, 45 pack-years. Reports 3 weeks of hemoptysis and an unintentional 6 kg weight loss. LDCT 'screening' ordered. A counseling and shared decision-making visit was documented 2 weeks ago: eligibility was confirmed, a decision aid was used, adherence to annual screening and comorbidities were discussed, and smoking cessation counseling was provided. Order on file from the primary care physician for lung cancer screening with LDCT. Reading radiologist is ABR board-certified. The imaging center reports nodules using Lung-RADS.
cases.note: Symptomatic patient: imaging would be diagnostic, not a screening service under this NCD.

cases.vignette: 60-year-old woman, current smoker, 1 pack/day for 40 years. Asymptomatic. This would be her first LDCT screening. The chart contains the order but no record of a counseling or shared decision-making visit. Order on file from the primary care physician for lung cancer screening with LDCT. Reading radiologist is ABR board-certified. The imaging center reports nodules using Lung-RADS.
cases.note: First screening with no documented counseling/shared decision-making visit.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old man, quit 6 years ago after 50 pack-years. Asymptomatic. His last LDCT screening was 13 months ago with a Lung-RADS 2 result; annual repeat screening requested. The shared decision-making visit was documented before his first screening 2 years ago. Order on file from the primary care physician for lung cancer screening with LDCT. Reading radiologist is ABR board-certified. The imaging center reports nodules using Lung-RADS.
cases.note: Repeat annual screening: C6 applies only before the first screening.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension who reports 2 months of exertional chest pressure, suspected to be coronary artery disease. Her cardiologist orders a rest and regadenoson pharmacological-stress PET myocardial perfusion study using FDA-approved Rubidium-82 as her initial stress imaging test, instead of a SPECT study. No SPECT has been performed or is planned.
cases.note: Suspected CAD; rest/pharmacological-stress Rb-82 PET in place of SPECT (no SPECT done).

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman with obesity and suspected coronary artery disease. A pharmacological-stress SPECT study 3 weeks ago was reported as technically uninterpretable because of severe soft-tissue attenuation, and that report is in her file. Her cardiologist documents that a PET study is necessary to decide whether she needs coronary angiography and revascularization or medical therapy alone, and orders a rest and dipyridamole-stress PET perfusion study using FDA-approved ammonia N-13.
cases.note: Ammonia N-13 PET after a SPECT that was technically uninterpretable (documented), with PET needed to decide between revascularization and medical therapy.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old man with exertional angina. A pharmacological-stress SPECT study 2 weeks ago was technically excellent and clearly showed a moderate reversible inferior perfusion defect, consistent with his symptoms and ECG findings; the report calls the study diagnostic. His cardiologist orders a rest and regadenoson-stress Rubidium-82 PET study 'to confirm the SPECT findings' before deciding on catheterization.
cases.note: PET added to a conclusive SPECT only to confirm it: not in place of SPECT and not after an inconclusive SPECT.

cases.vignette: 65-year-old man with suspected coronary artery disease and atypical chest pain. His cardiologist orders a PET myocardial perfusion study with FDA-approved Rubidium-82, performed at rest and with treadmill exercise stress, as his initial stress imaging test in place of SPECT. No SPECT has been performed.
cases.note: Treadmill exercise-stress PET; the NCD covers only rest or pharmacological-stress PET.

cases.vignette: 82-year-old man with known coronary artery disease treated medically. A pharmacological-stress SPECT study last month was reported as equivocal, and the report is in his file. He has repeatedly declined catheterization, revascularization and any change in his medications. His cardiologist documents that the PET result will not change his treatment and orders a rest and regadenoson-stress Rubidium-82 PET study 'for completeness of the record.'
cases.note: Prior SPECT was documented as equivocal, but PET is not considered necessary to determine any intervention: the patient has declined all interventions and the cardiologist documents it will not change management.

cases.vignette: 76-year-old man with known coronary artery disease and coronary artery bypass grafting 8 years ago, now with recurrent angina. A pharmacological-stress SPECT study 1 month ago showed no perfusion defect, which is discordant with a recent angiogram showing a severely narrowed vein graft; the cardiologist documents this discordance in his file. The cardiologist documents that PET is needed to decide whether repeat revascularization is required, and orders a Rubidium-82 PET perfusion study at rest followed by regadenoson pharmacological stress.
cases.note: Rest-only Rb-82 PET in known CAD after a SPECT discordant with angiography (inconclusive by definition), documented, with PET needed to decide on repeat revascularization.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old woman with suspected coronary artery disease. Her cardiologist's note states that a SPECT study at an outside facility 'was not helpful' and that a PET study is needed to decide whether she should undergo catheterization. The SPECT report is not in her file, and the file contains no description of the SPECT results. The cardiologist orders a rest and regadenoson-stress Rubidium-82 PET perfusion study.
cases.note: PET ordered after a prior SPECT said to be unhelpful, but no SPECT report or documentation of an equivocal, uninterpretable or discordant result is in the file.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman with pulmonary sarcoidosis and new heart block. Coronary angiography 3 months ago showed normal coronary arteries, and her cardiologist documents that coronary artery disease is not suspected. To evaluate suspected cardiac sarcoidosis, the cardiologist orders a resting Rubidium-82 PET myocardial perfusion study. No SPECT has been performed.
cases.note: Coronary artery disease is neither known nor suspected (normal coronary angiogram 3 months ago); the PET perfusion study is for suspected cardiac sarcoidosis, outside this NCD's indication.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with known coronary artery disease and a drug-eluting stent placed 4 years ago, with a BMI of 42 kg/m2 and left bundle branch block, now with new exertional dyspnea. His cardiologist orders a rest and regadenoson pharmacological-stress PET myocardial perfusion study using FDA-approved Rubidium-82 instead of a SPECT study. No SPECT has been performed.
cases.note: Known CAD with a prior stent; pharmacological-stress Rb-82 PET in place of SPECT. Obesity and left bundle branch block are distractors.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old man with suspected coronary artery disease and exertional chest discomfort. His cardiologist orders a 'cardiac PET perfusion study, rest and pharmacological stress' as his initial stress imaging test in place of SPECT. No SPECT has been performed. The order, the scheduling record and the imaging center's protocol sheet do not name the radiopharmaceutical to be used.
cases.note: The radiopharmaceutical is not specified anywhere, so use of an FDA-approved Rb-82 or ammonia N-13 agent cannot be confirmed.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old man diagnosed with dementia two months ago. His wife reports that 14 months ago he began making inappropriate comments to strangers and lost the ability to manage the household finances, followed by forgetfulness. A behavioral neurologist who specializes in dementia performed a comprehensive evaluation: history from the patient and his wife including activities of daily living, physical and neurological examination, Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores of 24 fourteen months ago and 19 now (formal documentation of decline over 14 months), neuropsychological testing showing both executive and memory deficits, normal B12 and thyroid-stimulating hormone, and a brain MRI with generalized atrophy and no stroke or mass. He meets diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia; the neurologist documents that early disinhibition makes FTD a suspected alternative cause, that the evaluation did not establish a specific cause, and that FDG PET is expected to distinguish FTD from AD and guide treatment. He has never had a brain SPECT or PET scan. The record documents the date of symptom onset, the clinical syndrome (mild dementia), the cognitive scores, the presumptive cause (uncertain AD), the neuropsychological results, the MRI report, the laboratory results, and his three prescribed medications by name. The scan will be performed at a hospital nuclear medicine department with all necessary accreditation and read by a nuclear medicine physician experienced in interpreting dementia PET scans.
cases.note: All B.1 conditions met and all record items present; no prior SPECT or PET.

cases.vignette: 59-year-old woman with treated hypertension, diagnosed with dementia last month. Her husband reports progressive word-finding difficulty and poor planning, followed by forgetfulness. A geriatric psychiatrist experienced in dementia assessment performed a comprehensive evaluation: history from the patient and her husband including activities of daily living, physical and mental status examination, Mini-Mental State Examination scores of 27 exactly 6 months ago and 22 now (formal documentation of decline over 6 months), neuropsychological testing, normal B12 and thyroid studies, and a brain CT without stroke, hydrocephalus or mass. She meets diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia; the psychiatrist documents that early language difficulty raises suspicion of FTD, that the cause remains uncertain after evaluation, and that FDG PET is expected to clarify FTD versus AD and guide treatment. She has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The record contains the onset date, clinical syndrome (mild dementia), MMSE scores, presumptive cause (possible AD), neuropsychological results, CT report, laboratory results, and the names of her two medications. The scan will be done at an imaging center with all accreditation required to operate nuclear medicine equipment and read by a neuroradiologist experienced with dementia PET.
cases.note: Boundary: cognitive decline documented over exactly 6 months ('at least 6 months'). Early-onset age and treated hypertension are distractors.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man diagnosed with dementia three weeks ago. His daughter reports that 4 months ago he became socially disinhibited and began having trouble organizing tasks, then started forgetting appointments; she is certain there were no problems before that. A cognitive neurologist experienced in dementia performed a comprehensive evaluation: history from the patient and his daughter including activities of daily living, examination, MoCA scores of 25 four months ago and 20 now, neuropsychological testing, normal B12 and thyroid studies, and a brain MRI without stroke or mass. He meets diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia; the neurologist documents that FTD is suspected given early disinhibition, that the cause remains uncertain, and that FDG PET would help distinguish FTD from AD and guide treatment. He has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The record contains all required elements, including onset date, syndrome, scores, presumptive cause, testing, imaging, labs and medication list. The scan will be done at an accredited nuclear medicine facility and read by an experienced nuclear medicine physician.
cases.note: Cognitive decline documented over only 4 months; the NCD requires at least 6 months.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old woman with dementia meeting diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia, with cognitive decline documented over 2 years. An FDG PET of the brain 15 months ago was read as inconclusive. Since then she has had a marked worsening, with new apathy, compulsive eating and loss of the ability to dress herself, and her MMSE has fallen from 24 to 16. Her dementia-specialist neurologist repeated a comprehensive evaluation: history from the patient and her son including activities of daily living, examination, serial cognitive scales, updated neuropsychological testing, normal B12 and thyroid studies, and a new brain MRI without stroke or mass. The neurologist documents that FTD is suspected as an alternative cause, that the specific cause remains uncertain, and that a new FDG PET is expected to clarify FTD versus AD and guide treatment. The record contains the onset date, clinical syndrome (moderate dementia), MMSE scores, presumptive cause (uncertain AD), neuropsychological results, MRI report, laboratory results, and the names of her four medications. The scan will be performed at an accredited hospital nuclear medicine department and read by an experienced nuclear medicine physician.
cases.note: Repeat exception: prior FDG PET 15 months ago was inconclusive, there is an important change in severity, diagnosis remains uncertain, and more than one year has passed.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old man with dementia meeting diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia, with cognitive decline documented over 20 months. An FDG PET of the brain 8 months ago was read as inconclusive. Since then he has developed prominent disinhibition and his MoCA has fallen from 22 to 15. His dementia-specialist neurologist repeated a comprehensive evaluation: history from the patient and his wife including activities of daily living, examination, serial cognitive scales, neuropsychological testing, normal B12 and thyroid studies, and a repeat MRI without new findings. The neurologist documents that FTD is suspected as an alternative cause, that the cause remains uncertain, and that a new FDG PET would help clarify FTD versus AD and guide treatment. The record contains all required elements, including onset date, syndrome, scores, presumptive cause, testing, imaging, labs and medication list. The scan would be done at an accredited nuclear medicine facility and read by an experienced nuclear medicine physician.
cases.note: Prior FDG PET was inconclusive and there is a change in severity, but only 8 months have passed; the exception requires one year.

cases.vignette: 79-year-old woman diagnosed with dementia three months ago after 2 years of gradually worsening short-term memory loss; her family reports no change in personality, behavior, language or social conduct. A memory-clinic neurologist experienced in dementia performed a comprehensive evaluation including informant history with activities of daily living, examination, serial MMSE scores of 25 and 21 over 2 years, neuropsychological testing showing an amnestic pattern, normal B12 and thyroid studies, and an MRI with hippocampal atrophy. The neurologist's assessment is 'probable Alzheimer's disease, clinically typical; no features to suggest frontotemporal dementia.' An FDG PET is requested to confirm the Alzheimer's diagnosis before starting a new medication. She has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The record contains all of the listed documentation elements. The scan would be performed at an accredited nuclear medicine facility and read by an experienced nuclear medicine physician.
cases.note: Clinically typical probable AD with no features suggesting FTD; PET requested only to confirm AD, which is a non-covered use.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment diagnosed 8 months ago; he remains fully independent in activities of daily living and does not meet criteria for dementia. His neurologist, who is experienced in dementia, documented mild memory and executive decline over 10 months on serial MoCA testing, with normal B12 and thyroid studies and an unremarkable MRI. The neurologist requests an FDG PET to estimate his risk of progressing to Alzheimer's disease or frontotemporal dementia. He is not enrolled in any clinical trial. He has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The scan would be performed at an accredited nuclear medicine facility.
cases.note: Mild cognitive impairment, not dementia meeting AD and FTD criteria; outside B.1, FDG PET is covered only in an approved clinical trial, and he is not enrolled in one.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old woman diagnosed with dementia two months ago, with early loss of executive function and socially inappropriate behavior followed by memory loss over the past 11 months. A behavioral neurologist experienced in dementia performed a comprehensive evaluation: history from the patient and her sister including activities of daily living, examination, MoCA scores of 26 eleven months ago and 20 now, neuropsychological testing, normal B12 and thyroid studies, and an MRI without stroke or mass. She meets diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia; the neurologist documents that FTD is suspected, that the cause remains uncertain, and that FDG PET is expected to clarify FTD versus AD and guide treatment. She has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The record contains all of the listed documentation elements. The scan is scheduled on a mobile PET unit whose nuclear medicine accreditation lapsed four months ago and has not been renewed; the images would be read by a nuclear medicine physician experienced with dementia scans.
cases.note: Every clinical criterion is met, but the mobile imaging unit lacks the accreditation needed to operate nuclear medicine equipment.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man diagnosed with dementia six weeks ago, with early language difficulty and poor judgment followed by forgetfulness over the past 12 months. A dementia-specialist neurologist performed a comprehensive evaluation: history from the patient and his wife including activities of daily living, examination, MMSE scores of 26 twelve months ago and 21 now, neuropsychological testing, normal B12 and thyroid-stimulating hormone, and an MRI without stroke or mass. He meets diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia; the neurologist documents that FTD is suspected, that the cause remains uncertain, and that FDG PET is expected to distinguish FTD from AD and guide treatment. He has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The record contains the onset date, clinical syndrome (mild dementia), MMSE scores, presumptive cause (uncertain AD), neuropsychological results, MRI report and laboratory results; the medication section of the record is blank and no medication list appears anywhere in the chart. The scan will be performed at an accredited nuclear medicine facility and read by an experienced nuclear medicine physician.
cases.note: Clinical criteria are met, but the record lacks the number and names of prescribed medications, one of the items providers must maintain.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman diagnosed with dementia last month, with early apathy and loss of executive function followed by memory loss over the past 9 months. A geriatric neurologist experienced in dementia evaluated her: history from the patient and her daughter including activities of daily living, examination, MoCA scores of 25 nine months ago and 19 now, neuropsychological testing, and normal B12 and thyroid studies. She meets diagnostic criteria for both Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia; the neurologist documents that FTD is suspected, that the cause remains uncertain, and that FDG PET is expected to clarify FTD versus AD and guide treatment. She has had no prior brain SPECT or PET. The record contains the onset date, syndrome, scores, presumptive cause, neuropsychological results, laboratory results and her medication list, but contains no brain MRI or CT report and no mention of whether structural imaging was performed. The scan will be done at an accredited nuclear medicine facility and read by an experienced nuclear medicine physician.
cases.note: The comprehensive evaluation must include structural imaging; no MRI or CT report or mention appears in the record, and nothing indicates it was refused or contraindicated.

cases.vignette: 63-year-old woman with stress urinary incontinence (ICD-10-CM N39.3) using 4 pads daily. History and physical examination including a pelvic exam were completed. A simple cystometrogram showed normal bladder compliance and no abnormality of urethral support, and there is no urethral hypermobility on examination. An abdominal leak point pressure test with 200 cc in the bladder showed leakage at 72 cm H2O, establishing intrinsic sphincter deficiency. A collagen skin test was placed 5 weeks ago and evaluated over 4 weeks with no reaction. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. Periurethral collagen implant injection is requested; this would be her first session.
cases.note: Female with ISD: no hypermobility, ALPP 72 cm H2O; skin test and trained urologist documented.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old man with stress urinary incontinence (ICD-10-CM N39.3) since radical prostatectomy 2 years ago, using 3 pads daily. Complete history and physical examination were performed, and a simple cystometrogram showed the bladder fills and stores properly. Standing upright with a full bladder, he leaked with coughing, establishing intrinsic sphincter deficiency. A collagen skin test was placed 5 weeks ago and evaluated over 4 weeks with no reaction. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. Collagen implant injection is requested; he has had no prior injections.
cases.note: Male post-prostatectomy ISD established by standing cough leak; evaluation, skin test and training all documented.

cases.vignette: 58-year-old woman with stress urinary incontinence (ICD-10-CM N39.3). History and physical examination including a pelvic exam were completed; a simple cystometrogram showed normal bladder compliance. Examination and a Q-tip test show marked urethral hypermobility (resting-to-straining angle change of 50 degrees). Abdominal leak point pressure with 200 cc in the bladder was 80 cm H2O. A collagen skin test was placed 5 weeks ago and evaluated over 4 weeks with no reaction. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. Collagen implant injection is requested.
cases.note: Female with urethral hypermobility is excluded even though ALPP is low.

cases.vignette: 61-year-old woman with stress urinary incontinence (ICD-10-CM N39.3). History and physical examination including a pelvic exam were completed. A simple cystometrogram showed normal bladder compliance and no abnormality of urethral support, and there is no urethral hypermobility on examination. Abdominal leak point pressure with 250 cc in the bladder was 118 cm H2O. A collagen skin test was placed 5 weeks ago and evaluated over 4 weeks with no reaction. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. Collagen implant injection is requested.
cases.note: Female ALPP 118 cm H2O exceeds 100: ISD not established.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman with stress urinary incontinence (ICD-10-CM N39.3). History and physical examination including a pelvic exam were completed. A simple cystometrogram showed normal bladder compliance and no abnormality of urethral support, and there is no urethral hypermobility on examination. Abdominal leak point pressure with 200 cc in the bladder was 64 cm H2O. A collagen skin test was placed 7 days ago and read as negative at 1 week; the injection is scheduled for tomorrow. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. Collagen implant injection is requested.
cases.note: Skin test evaluated only 1 week, not over the required 4-week period.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old man with stress urinary incontinence after prostatectomy and radiation (ICD-10-CM N39.3), with ISD established by cystometrogram and a standing cough leak test. He has had 5 separate collagen injection sessions over the past 14 months, with no improvement in pad use (still 5 pads daily) after any of them. His original skin test was negative over 4 weeks. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. A sixth collagen implant session is requested.
cases.note: Sixth session after 5 sessions without improvement: treatment failure, no further collagen coverage.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with intrinsic sphincter deficiency established by cystometrogram (normal compliance and urethral support, no hypermobility) and an abdominal leak point pressure of 70 cm H2O. Two collagen injection sessions 10 months ago made her dry, and she stayed continent until 9 months after treatment, when stress leakage recurred. A repeat collagen skin test placed 5 weeks ago and evaluated over 4 weeks showed no reaction. Her urologist documents the prior success, the recurrence, a repeat history and physical examination including a pelvic exam confirming unchanged anatomy, and the medical justification for additional sessions. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. An additional collagen implant session is requested.
cases.note: Exception: recurrence 9 months after successful collagen treatment, with documented medical justification for additional sessions.

cases.vignette: 60-year-old woman with stress urinary incontinence (ICD-10-CM N39.3). History and physical examination including a pelvic exam were completed. A simple cystometrogram showed normal bladder compliance and no abnormality of urethral support, and there is no urethral hypermobility on examination. Abdominal leak point pressure with 200 cc in the bladder was 68 cm H2O, establishing intrinsic sphincter deficiency. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. Collagen implant injection is requested; the record contains no documentation of a collagen sensitivity skin test.
cases.note: All other requirements met, but no collagen skin test is documented.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with stress urinary incontinence after radical prostatectomy (ICD-10-CM N39.3). Complete history and physical examination were performed, a simple cystometrogram showed the bladder fills and stores properly, and he leaked with coughing while standing with a full bladder. A collagen skin test was placed 5 weeks ago and evaluated over 4 weeks with no reaction. The injecting urologist is experienced in cystoscopy but has not attended or completed any collagen implant training program. Collagen implant injection is requested.
cases.note: Injecting urologist has not completed a collagen implant training program.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old woman with stress urinary incontinence (ICD-10-CM N39.3). History and physical examination including a pelvic exam were completed and show no urethral hypermobility. An abdominal leak point pressure test with 200 cc in the bladder showed leakage at 75 cm H2O. No cystometrogram result appears in the record. A collagen skin test was placed 5 weeks ago and evaluated over 4 weeks with no reaction. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. Collagen implant injection is requested.
cases.note: Female with ALPP 75, but no cystometrogram documented to rule out compliance and support abnormalities.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with severe emphysema (ICD-10-CM J43.9) consistent with history and physical examination; BMI 26.4 kg/m2. He has been stable for 6 months on prednisone 5 mg daily. HRCT shows bilateral emphysema that the radiologist reads as severe and upper lobe predominant. Pre-rehabilitation pulmonary function: FEV1 27% predicted, DLCO 34% predicted, TLC 128% predicted and RV 215% predicted post-bronchodilator. Pre-rehabilitation room-air arterial blood gas at sea level: PCO2 44 mm Hg, PO2 63 mm Hg. Echocardiogram shows LVEF 60%; he is in sinus rhythm with no premature ventricular contractions on resting EKG and no angina. He completed an 8-week preoperative program of 18 sessions of 2.5 hours each, consistent with NETT, based on the treating physician's care plan after a comprehensive medical, psychosocial and nutritional evaluation and coordinated by the surgical facility; 7 postoperative sessions of 2 hours within 8 weeks after surgery are scheduled. Post-rehabilitation 6-minute walk is 265 m and he completed 3 minutes of unloaded pedaling before and after rehabilitation; maximal cycle ergometry workload after the program was 45 W. After rehabilitation, the pulmonologist, thoracic surgeon and anesthesiologist each documented approval for surgery. Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation are on file. He quit smoking 3 years ago; plasma cotinine is 3 ng/mL. Bilateral stapled lung volume reduction via video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery is planned at a hospital approved by Medicare as a lung transplantation hospital.
cases.note: All criteria met; upper-lobe-predominant disease, so exercise capacity (45 W) does not matter.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old woman with severe emphysema (ICD-10-CM J43.9) consistent with history and physical examination; BMI 29.8 kg/m2. She takes no systemic corticosteroids. HRCT shows bilateral severe emphysema that the radiologist reads as lower lobe predominant (non-upper lobe), with heterogeneous distribution. Pre-rehabilitation pulmonary function: FEV1 27% predicted, DLCO 34% predicted, TLC 128% predicted and RV 215% predicted post-bronchodilator. Pre-rehabilitation room-air arterial blood gas at sea level: PCO2 44 mm Hg, PO2 63 mm Hg. Echocardiogram shows LVEF 58%; she is in sinus rhythm with no premature ventricular contractions and no angina. She completed a 7-week preoperative program of 16 sessions of 2 hours each, consistent with NETT, based on the treating physician's care plan after a comprehensive medical, psychosocial and nutritional evaluation and coordinated by the surgical facility; 6 postoperative sessions of 2 hours within 8 weeks after surgery are scheduled. Post-rehabilitation 6-minute walk is 210 m and she completed 3 minutes of unloaded pedaling before and after rehabilitation; maximal cycle ergometry workload after the program (5 W/min ramp on 30% oxygen) was 25 W. After rehabilitation, the pulmonologist, thoracic surgeon and anesthesiologist each documented approval for surgery. Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation are on file. She quit smoking 18 months ago; plasma cotinine is 2 ng/mL. Bilateral stapled lung volume reduction via median sternotomy is planned at a hospital certified by the Joint Commission under the LVRS Disease Specific Care Certification Program.
cases.note: Boundary: woman with non-upper-lobe emphysema and maximal workload exactly 25 W (low exercise capacity).

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with severe emphysema (ICD-10-CM J43.9) consistent with history and physical examination; BMI 26.4 kg/m2. He has been stable for 6 months on prednisone 5 mg daily. HRCT shows bilateral emphysema that the radiologist reads as severe and upper lobe predominant. Pre-rehabilitation pulmonary function: FEV1 27% predicted, DLCO 34% predicted, TLC 128% predicted and RV 215% predicted post-bronchodilator. Pre-rehabilitation room-air arterial blood gas at sea level: PCO2 44 mm Hg, PO2 63 mm Hg. Echocardiogram shows LVEF 60%; he is in sinus rhythm with no premature ventricular contractions on resting EKG and no angina. He completed an 8-week preoperative program of 18 sessions of 2.5 hours each, consistent with NETT, based on the treating physician's care plan after a comprehensive medical, psychosocial and nutritional evaluation and coordinated by the surgical facility; 7 postoperative sessions of 2 hours within 8 weeks after surgery are scheduled. Post-rehabilitation 6-minute walk is 265 m and he completed 3 minutes of unloaded pedaling before and after rehabilitation; maximal cycle ergometry workload after the program was 45 W. After rehabilitation, the pulmonologist, thoracic surgeon and anesthesiologist each documented approval for surgery. Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation are on file. He quit smoking 3 years ago; plasma cotinine is 3 ng/mL. Bilateral stapled lung volume reduction via video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery is planned at a community hospital with an experienced thoracic surgery group; the hospital holds general Joint Commission accreditation but no LVRS Disease Specific Care certification and is not a Medicare-approved lung or heart-lung transplantation hospital.
cases.note: Surgery at a hospital that is neither Joint Commission LVRS-certified nor a Medicare-approved lung transplant hospital.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with severe emphysema (ICD-10-CM J43.9) consistent with history and physical examination; BMI 26.4 kg/m2. He has been stable for 6 months on prednisone 5 mg daily. HRCT shows bilateral emphysema that the radiologist reads as severe and upper lobe predominant. Pre-rehabilitation pulmonary function: FEV1 27% predicted, DLCO 34% predicted, TLC 128% predicted and RV 215% predicted post-bronchodilator. Pre-rehabilitation room-air arterial blood gas at sea level: PCO2 44 mm Hg, PO2 63 mm Hg. Echocardiogram shows LVEF 60%; he is in sinus rhythm with no premature ventricular contractions on resting EKG and no angina. He completed an 8-week preoperative program of 18 sessions of 2.5 hours each, consistent with NETT, based on the treating physician's care plan after a comprehensive medical, psychosocial and nutritional evaluation and coordinated by the surgical facility; 7 postoperative sessions of 2 hours within 8 weeks after surgery are scheduled. Post-rehabilitation 6-minute walk is 265 m and he completed 3 minutes of unloaded pedaling before and after rehabilitation; maximal cycle ergometry workload after the program was 45 W. After rehabilitation, the pulmonologist, thoracic surgeon and anesthesiologist each documented approval for surgery. Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation are on file. He reports quitting smoking 2 years ago; no plasma cotinine or carboxyhemoglobin test result is in the record. Bilateral stapled lung volume reduction via video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery is planned at a hospital approved by Medicare as a lung transplantation hospital.
cases.note: Patient reports quitting 2 years ago, but no plasma cotinine or carboxyhemoglobin result is in the record.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with severe emphysema (ICD-10-CM J43.9) consistent with history and physical examination; BMI 26.4 kg/m2. He has been stable for 6 months on prednisone 5 mg daily. HRCT shows bilateral emphysema that the radiologist reads as severe and upper lobe predominant. Pre-rehabilitation pulmonary function: FEV1 27% predicted, DLCO 34% predicted, TLC 128% predicted and RV 215% predicted post-bronchodilator. Pre-rehabilitation room-air arterial blood gas at sea level: PCO2 44 mm Hg, PO2 63 mm Hg. Echocardiogram shows LVEF 60%; he is in sinus rhythm with no premature ventricular contractions on resting EKG and no angina. He completed an 8-week preoperative program of 18 sessions of 2.5 hours each, consistent with NETT, based on the treating physician's care plan after a comprehensive medical, psychosocial and nutritional evaluation and coordinated by the surgical facility; 7 postoperative sessions of 2 hours within 8 weeks after surgery are scheduled. Post-rehabilitation 6-minute walk is 265 m and he completed 3 minutes of unloaded pedaling before and after rehabilitation; maximal cycle ergometry workload after the program was 45 W. After rehabilitation, the pulmonologist and thoracic surgeon documented approval for surgery; the record contains no anesthesiology evaluation or anesthesiologist approval. Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation are on file. He quit smoking 3 years ago; plasma cotinine is 3 ng/mL. Bilateral stapled lung volume reduction via video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery is planned at a hospital approved by Medicare as a lung transplantation hospital.
cases.note: Pulmonologist and surgeon approvals present; no anesthesiologist assessment or approval is documented.

cases.vignette: 74-year-old woman with COPD (ICD-10-CM J44.9) seen in her pulmonologist's office for worsening fatigue and morning headaches. The pulmonologist ordered pulse oximetry, which office staff performed under her supervision with the patient seated at rest breathing room air: SpO2 88%. The pulmonologist reviewed the result the same day and prescribes a home stationary oxygen concentrator at 2 L/min. She has no angina, peripheral vascular disease, or terminal illness.
cases.note: Boundary: SpO2 exactly 88% at rest on room air, ordered, evaluated, and supervised by the treating practitioner.

cases.vignette: 79-year-old man hospitalized for a COPD exacerbation with pneumonia. The day before discharge, his attending physician ordered an arterial blood gas at rest on room air, run by the hospital's certified blood gas laboratory: PaO2 54 mm Hg. A ward pulse oximetry reading taken at the same time showed SpO2 90%. The attending physician reviewed both, documented reliance on the blood gas, and prescribes home oxygen at discharge. He is not terminally ill and has no angina or peripheral vascular disease.
cases.note: ABG from a certified hospital lab the day before discharge qualifies; conflicting ward oximetry is outweighed because ABG is preferred.

cases.vignette: 71-year-old man with obesity hypoventilation and COPD. His primary care physician ordered resting room-air pulse oximetry, performed in her office under her supervision during a period of worsening daytime somnolence: SpO2 89%. A CBC the same week shows hematocrit 57% (erythrocythemia). There is no dependent edema and an echocardiogram shows normal pulmonary pressures. She reviewed the results and prescribes home oxygen.
cases.note: Group II boundary: SpO2 exactly 89% with hematocrit 57% (> 56%).

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer to both lungs and a malignant pleural effusion, enrolled in hospice with a life expectancy of weeks. She has progressive dyspnea at rest. Her hospice physician ordered and personally performed resting room-air pulse oximetry at a home visit: SpO2 85%. He evaluated the result and prescribes home oxygen.
cases.note: Terminal illness that affects breathing (lung metastases) with qualifying resting hypoxemia; the hospice setting is a distractor.

cases.vignette: 76-year-old man with chronic stable angina who has chest pressure two to three times a week on exertion, relieved by nitroglycerin. His cardiologist ordered and evaluated an arterial blood gas at rest on room air (PaO2 82 mm Hg) and an exercise oximetry test (lowest SpO2 95%). He has no lung disease. The cardiologist prescribes home oxygen to use during angina episodes.
cases.note: Angina without hypoxemia is a national non-coverage.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with deconditioning and anxiety who reports breathlessness when climbing stairs. Physician-ordered testing, evaluated by her internist, shows SpO2 95% at rest on room air, a lowest SpO2 of 93% during a 6-minute walk, and no desaturation below 92% on overnight oximetry. Echocardiogram shows normal right heart size and pulmonary pressures; there is no edema. Her internist prescribes home oxygen 'as needed for shortness of breath.'
cases.note: Breathlessness with normal saturation at rest, exertion, and sleep and no cor pulmonale.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old man with severe peripheral arterial disease and a non-healing ischemic ulcer of the left foot. Pulse oximetry on the left toes reads 84%, while a physician-ordered arterial blood gas at rest on room air, evaluated by his vascular surgeon, shows PaO2 88 mm Hg and a right-finger SpO2 of 97%. The vascular surgeon prescribes home oxygen to improve oxygen delivery to the foot.
cases.note: Desaturation is limited to an ischemic limb from severe PVD; systemic oxygenation is normal.

cases.vignette: 82-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer to bone, enrolled in hospice. He has bone pain but no lung involvement and no dyspnea. His hospice physician ordered and evaluated resting room-air oximetry, SpO2 95%. The family asks for home oxygen for comfort, and the hospice physician prescribes it.
cases.note: Terminal illness that does not affect breathing, with normal saturation.

cases.vignette: 77-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and progressive dyspnea on exertion. Her pulmonologist's note states 'hypoxemic, needs home oxygen' and prescribes a stationary concentrator and portable system. The submitted record contains the clinic note, a CT report showing fibrosis, and pulmonary function tests, but no arterial blood gas or oximetry result.
cases.note: No oximetry or blood gas result in the record; nothing shows the patient is not hypoxemic.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with COPD seen by his primary care physician, who ordered pulse oximetry in her office and reviewed the result: SpO2 87%. The record does not state whether the reading was taken at rest or during activity, or whether he was breathing room air or using supplemental oxygen at the time. He has no angina, peripheral vascular disease, or terminal illness. She prescribes home oxygen.
cases.note: SpO2 87% is recorded, but whether at rest and whether on room air is not documented.

cases.vignette: 58-year-old man. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Attended polysomnography in a sleep laboratory showed an AHI of 22 events/hour over 6.5 hours of sleep. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
cases.note: Typical qualifying case: AHI 22 on attended PSG.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with documented hypertension on two medications. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by her physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Unattended home sleep test with a Type III device showed an AHI of 9 events/hour. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by her treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before she began using the device.
cases.note: AHI 9 (5-14 band) qualifies because hypertension is documented.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man without hypertension, heart disease, or stroke; he denies daytime sleepiness. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Attended PSG showed an AHI of 15.0 events/hour over 7 hours of sleep. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
cases.note: Boundary: AHI exactly 15 qualifies without symptoms or comorbidities (>= 15).

cases.vignette: 61-year-old man. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. He denies daytime sleepiness, insomnia, mood or memory problems; blood pressure is normal and he has no history of heart disease or stroke. Type III home sleep test showed an AHI of 9 events/hour. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
cases.note: AHI 9 with no qualifying symptom or comorbidity documented.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old woman. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by her physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Overnight pulse oximetry at home showed an oxygen desaturation index of 25 events/hour. No polysomnography or home sleep apnea test was performed. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The oximetry was ordered by her treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before she began using the device.
cases.note: Overnight pulse oximetry alone is not a qualifying test.

cases.vignette: 59-year-old man. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Unattended home sleep test with a Type IV device recording 2 channels (oximetry and heart rate) reported an AHI of 28 events/hour. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
cases.note: Type IV device with only 2 channels does not qualify (needs at least 3).

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with no hypertension, heart disease, stroke, or sleep-related symptoms documented. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by her physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Attended PSG recorded only 1.5 hours of continuous sleep with 25 apneas and hypopneas in total (reported AHI 16.7 events/hour). Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by her treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before she began using the device.
cases.note: 1.5 h of sleep with 25 events: AHI 16.7, but 2 h at >=15/h requires >=30 events.

cases.vignette: 63-year-old man. Attended PSG ordered by his treating physician showed an AHI of 31 events/hour. The record contains the sleep study report and CPAP order, but no clinical evaluation by a physician. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
cases.note: Qualifying test but no clinical evaluation in the record.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man diagnosed with OSA (AHI 24 on attended PSG after a documented clinical evaluation) who completed the initial 12-week CPAP period. He used the device on only a few nights, reports no improvement in sleepiness, and his physician documents no clinical benefit from CPAP. Requesting continued CPAP coverage beyond 12 weeks. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
cases.note: Continued coverage after 12 weeks requires benefit; physician documents none.

cases.vignette: 78-year-old man with mild dementia who lives with his daughter, who is home every night and was trained by the DME supplier to operate the CPAP device safely. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Attended PSG showed an AHI of 34 events/hour. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period.
cases.note: Caregiver compensates for patient's limited capacity (allowed by C2).

cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman with severe COPD (FEV1 32% predicted). Awake arterial blood gas on her prescribed 2 L/min oxygen shows PaCO2 58 mmHg. No respiratory symptom change and no medication change for the past 6 weeks. Her pulmonologist documents that sleep apnea is not the predominant cause of her hypercapnia; no formal sleep study was done. Requesting a respiratory assist device with backup rate for an initial 6-month period.
cases.note: Stable hypercapnic COPD; clinician excludes sleep apnea without a formal sleep study (allowed).

cases.vignette: 71-year-old man with severe COPD. Awake arterial blood gas on his prescribed 2 L/min oxygen shows PaCO2 49 mmHg. Stable without symptom or medication changes for 2 months; his pulmonologist documents that sleep apnea is not the predominant cause of his hypercapnia. Requesting a respiratory assist device with backup rate for an initial 6-month period.
cases.note: PaCO2 49 is below 52.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman with severe COPD. Over the past 5 days she has had increased dyspnea and new purulent sputum, and her clinician started prednisone and an antibiotic 5 days ago; she was not hospitalized. Awake arterial blood gas on prescribed 2 L/min oxygen today shows PaCO2 57 mmHg. Sleep apnea is not the predominant cause of her hypercapnia per her pulmonologist. Requesting a respiratory assist device with backup rate for an initial 6-month period.
cases.note: Active exacerbation: increased dyspnea and purulent sputum, prednisone started 5 days ago.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old man with mild COPD (FEV1 68% predicted), BMI 46, and severe obstructive sleep apnea (AHI 64) on polysomnography. Awake arterial blood gas on room air shows PaCO2 55 mmHg. His pulmonologist documents that sleep apnea and obesity hypoventilation are the predominant cause of his hypercapnia. Stable for 2 months. Requesting a respiratory assist device with backup rate for COPD.
cases.note: Severe OSA with obesity hypoventilation is the predominant cause.

cases.vignette: 73-year-old woman hospitalized for acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure due to COPD. She required noninvasive ventilation with a respiratory assist device through the night before discharge, and her treating clinician documents a high risk of rapid symptom exacerbation and rising PaCO2 after discharge. Requesting a respiratory assist device in the home immediately upon discharge for an initial 6-month period.
cases.note: Discharge pathway: on BiPAP within 24 h of discharge with documented risk.

cases.vignette: 69-year-old man with COPD and chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure who began a respiratory assist device with backup rate 6 months ago (IPAP 18 cm H2O, backup rate 16). At his 6-month evaluation, device download shows an average of 5.5 hours per night on 80% of days over the last 30 days. PaCO2 fell from 58 to 52 mmHg, and his morning headaches and sleep quality have improved. Requesting continued coverage.
cases.note: Continuation: 5.5 h/night on 80% of days, improved headache and sleep quality.

cases.vignette: 70-year-old woman with COPD who began a respiratory assist device with backup rate 6 months ago. At her 6-month evaluation, device download shows use of at least 4 hours per 24 hours on 55% of days over the last 30 days. Her fatigue has improved somewhat. Requesting continued coverage.
cases.note: Continuation: 4+ hours on only 55% of days.

cases.vignette: 72-year-old man with COPD who began a respiratory assist device with backup rate 6 months ago. Device download shows 6 hours per night on 85% of days over the last 30 days. PaCO2 has continued to rise, from 56 to 61 mmHg, and his headache, fatigue, dyspnea, confusion and sleep quality are unchanged. Requesting continued coverage.
cases.note: Continuation: good usage but PaCO2 still rising and no symptom improvement.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with very severe COPD. Awake arterial blood gas on her prescribed 5 L/min nasal oxygen shows PaCO2 63 mmHg. Stable without symptom or medication changes for 1 month; her pulmonologist documents that sleep apnea is not the predominant cause. Requesting a home mechanical ventilator in a volume-targeted mode for an initial 6-month period.
cases.note: Home mechanical ventilator: hypercapnic, stable, and needs 5 L/min oxygen (>= 4 L).

cases.vignette: 74-year-old man with severe COPD. Awake arterial blood gas on his prescribed 1 L/min oxygen shows PaCO2 52 mmHg. No symptom or medication changes for 3 months; his pulmonologist documents that sleep apnea is not the predominant cause of his hypercapnia. Requesting a respiratory assist device with backup rate for an initial 6-month period.
cases.note: Boundary: PaCO2 exactly 52 meets >= 52.

cases.vignette: 61-year-old man with decompensated alcohol-associated cirrhosis (ICD-10-CM K70.31) with refractory ascites, two episodes of hepatic encephalopathy and a MELD-Na score of 27. He has been abstinent from alcohol for 14 months. He is listed for deceased-donor liver transplantation at a liver transplant center approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria.
cases.note: Non-malignant end-stage liver disease at a CMS-approved center.

cases.vignette: 57-year-old woman with end-stage liver disease due to chronic hepatitis B (ICD-10-CM B18.1) with cirrhosis, variceal bleeding and jaundice despite tenofovir therapy; imaging shows no liver mass. Liver transplantation is requested at a liver transplant center approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria.
cases.note: End-stage liver disease from hepatitis B: the pre-December 1999 hepatitis B exclusion no longer applies.

cases.vignette: 66-year-old man with hepatitis C cirrhosis and a single hepatocellular carcinoma (ICD-10-CM C22.0) measuring 5.0 cm in greatest diameter. Because of portal hypertension and Child-Pugh class B liver function, the hepatobiliary surgeon documents that he is not a candidate for subtotal liver resection. Triple-phase CT of the abdomen and CT of the chest and bone scan 3 weeks ago show no macrovascular invasion and no spread to lymph nodes, lungs, other abdominal organs or bone. The transplant would be performed at a liver transplant center approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria.
cases.note: HCC boundary: single 5.0 cm tumor meets <= 5 cm; not a resection candidate; no macrovascular or extrahepatic disease; approved center.

cases.vignette: 63-year-old woman with NASH cirrhosis and a single hepatocellular carcinoma (ICD-10-CM C22.0) measuring 5.6 cm. The hepatobiliary surgeon documents that she is not a candidate for subtotal liver resection because of portal hypertension. Triple-phase CT of the abdomen and CT of the chest and bone scan 3 weeks ago show no macrovascular invasion and no spread to lymph nodes, lungs, other abdominal organs or bone. The transplant would be performed at a liver transplant center approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria.
cases.note: HCC 5.6 cm exceeds the 5 cm limit.

cases.vignette: 68-year-old man with alcohol-associated cirrhosis and two hepatocellular carcinoma nodules (ICD-10-CM C22.0) of 2.8 cm and 1.9 cm. The hepatobiliary surgeon documents that he is not a candidate for subtotal liver resection. Triple-phase CT shows enhancing tumor thrombus in the right portal vein; chest CT and bone scan show no spread to lymph nodes, lungs, other abdominal organs or bone. The transplant would be performed at a liver transplant center approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria.
cases.note: Tumor thrombus in the right portal vein is macrovascular involvement.

cases.vignette: 62-year-old man with compensated Child-Pugh A cirrhosis from hepatitis C (sustained virologic response), normal bilirubin, no portal hypertension, and a single 3.2 cm peripheral hepatocellular carcinoma (ICD-10-CM C22.0) in segment 6. The hepatobiliary surgeon documents that he is a good candidate for a segmental (subtotal) liver resection with adequate future liver remnant, but the patient prefers transplantation. Triple-phase CT of the abdomen and CT of the chest and bone scan 3 weeks ago show no macrovascular invasion and no spread to lymph nodes, lungs, other abdominal organs or bone. The transplant would be performed at a liver transplant center approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria.
cases.note: Patient is a candidate for resection (well-compensated, peripheral tumor) but prefers transplant.

cases.vignette: 59-year-old woman with unresectable liver-only metastases from colon adenocarcinoma (ICD-10-CM C78.7), stable for 12 months on chemotherapy after resection of the primary tumor; no extrahepatic disease on PET-CT. Her oncologist requests liver transplantation at a CMS-approved liver transplant center.
cases.note: Colorectal cancer liver metastases are an 'other malignancy' and excluded.

cases.vignette: 54-year-old man with end-stage liver disease from primary sclerosing cholangitis (ICD-10-CM K83.01) with recurrent cholangitis and a MELD-Na of 24. Transplantation is requested at a university hospital that recently started a liver transplant program; the hospital has not been approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria for liver transplantation.
cases.note: Non-malignant ESLD, but the transplant hospital is not CMS-approved for liver transplantation.

cases.vignette: 60-year-old woman who received a Medicare-covered deceased-donor liver transplant for autoimmune hepatitis cirrhosis 9 days ago at a CMS-approved liver transplant center. She developed hepatic artery thrombosis with graft failure, rising transaminases and coagulopathy. Urgent liver re-transplantation at the same center is requested.
cases.note: Re-transplantation needed as a result of a covered liver transplant is covered.

cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with hepatitis B cirrhosis and a single 3.5 cm hepatocellular carcinoma (ICD-10-CM C22.0). The hepatobiliary surgeon documents that he is not a candidate for subtotal liver resection because of portal hypertension. Triple-phase abdominal MRI shows no macrovascular invasion and no abdominal lymphadenopathy. No chest imaging or bone imaging has been performed, and the record does not address the lungs or bone. The transplant would be performed at a liver transplant center approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria.
cases.note: HCC within size, not resectable, no macrovascular involvement on liver imaging, but no chest or bone staging documented to exclude extrahepatic spread.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with NASH cirrhosis and two hepatocellular carcinoma nodules (ICD-10-CM C22.0) of 2.1 cm and 1.6 cm. Triple-phase CT of the abdomen and CT of the chest and bone scan 3 weeks ago show no macrovascular invasion and no spread to lymph nodes, lungs, other abdominal organs or bone. The transplant would be performed at a liver transplant center approved by CMS as meeting institutional coverage criteria. The referral is from her hepatologist; no surgical consultation has taken place and the record does not address whether she is a candidate for liver resection.
cases.note: HCC otherwise within criteria, but the record contains no surgical assessment of resectability.

cases.vignette: 52-year-old man with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.22) and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis for 14 months. A simultaneous kidney and whole-organ pancreas transplant from a deceased donor is planned at a Medicare-approved transplant center. He started seeing an endocrinologist only 3 months ago and has not had hospitalizations for hypoglycemia or ketoacidosis. The transplant team finds him a suitable candidate.
cases.note: Simultaneous pancreas-kidney: PA-only criteria (12-month endocrinology management etc.) do not apply.

cases.vignette: 58-year-old woman with insulin-requiring type 2 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E11.22) who received a living-donor kidney transplant 3 years ago for diabetic nephropathy, with stable graft function on tacrolimus and mycophenolate. A whole-organ pancreas-after-kidney transplant is requested at the Medicare-approved center that performed her kidney transplant. The transplant team finds her a suitable candidate.
cases.note: Whole-organ pancreas after kidney transplant; the NCD does not restrict pancreas-after-kidney by diabetes type (type 2 is a distractor).

cases.vignette: 41-year-old woman with insulin-dependent diabetes since age 12 (ICD-10-CM E10.649), requesting a pancreas transplant alone. Beta cell autoantibodies (GAD65, IA-2, ZnT8) are negative. Fasting C-peptide is 0.88 ng/mL (laboratory lower limit of normal 0.80 ng/mL) with a concurrently drawn fasting glucose of 160 mg/dL. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
cases.note: Pancreas alone. Boundary: fasting C-peptide exactly 110% of the lab's lower limit of normal (0.88 vs LLN 0.80) with concurrent glucose 160 mg/dL.

cases.vignette: 36-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes since age 9 (ICD-10-CM E10.649), requesting a pancreas transplant alone. GAD65 autoantibodies are positive. A fasting C-peptide of 0.6 ng/mL (laboratory lower limit of normal 0.8 ng/mL) was drawn with a concurrent fasting glucose of 310 mg/dL. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
cases.note: Pancreas alone with positive GAD65 antibodies; the C-peptide drawn at glucose 310 is invalid but irrelevant because autoantibody positivity alone establishes type 1 diabetes.

cases.vignette: 48-year-old woman with insulin-treated diabetes diagnosed at age 30, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. Beta cell autoantibodies are negative on two panels. Fasting C-peptide is 1.2 ng/mL (laboratory lower limit of normal 0.8 ng/mL) with a concurrent fasting glucose of 130 mg/dL. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
cases.note: Antibody-negative and C-peptide 1.5x LLN with valid glucose: type 1 diabetes not established for pancreas alone.

cases.vignette: 39-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649) and positive GAD65 and IA-2 autoantibodies, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. The transplant would be performed at a hospital that is Medicare-approved for liver and heart transplantation but is not Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
cases.note: Pancreas alone at a center approved only for liver and heart transplantation, not kidney.

cases.vignette: 44-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649) and positive GAD65 autoantibodies, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Her primary care physician managed her diabetes until 8 months ago; since then she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
cases.note: Pancreas alone after only 8 months of endocrinologist management (needs >= 12 months).

cases.vignette: 45-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649) and positive GAD65 autoantibodies, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin. She has glucose variability and about two mild hypoglycemic episodes per month that she treats herself at home; she has never been hospitalized, seen in an emergency department or had ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and can manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the team finds her otherwise suitable. Her kidney function is normal and she has never had a kidney transplant.
cases.note: Pancreas alone: mild hypoglycemic episodes managed at home; no complications requiring hospitalization.

cases.vignette: 50-year-old man with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649), positive autoantibodies, severe hypoglycemia unawareness and three hospitalizations for severe hypoglycemia this year despite 3 years of endocrinologist management with a pump and continuous glucose monitor. His endocrinologist requests allogeneic pancreatic islet cell transplantation at a kidney-transplant-approved center as standard clinical care; he is not enrolled in any clinical trial.
cases.note: Islet cell transplantation outside a clinical trial is non-covered.

cases.vignette: 42-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E10.649) and positive GAD65 autoantibodies, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. The transplant surgeon's note finds her medically suitable; the record contains no psychosocial or psychological evaluation and no assessment of her understanding of surgical risks or ability to manage lifelong immunosuppression. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
cases.note: Pancreas alone with all clinical criteria met, but no assessment of emotional/mental capacity is documented.

cases.vignette: 38-year-old woman with insulin-dependent diabetes since age 15, requesting a pancreas transplant alone. Beta cell autoantibody testing was sent last week and results are pending; no fasting C-peptide has been measured. The transplant would be performed at a center that is Medicare-approved for kidney transplantation. Over the past 2 years she has been managed by an endocrinologist with a continuous glucose monitor, an automated insulin pump and rapid-acting analog insulin, yet she has had frequent hypoglycemia unawareness and four admissions in the last 18 months for severe hypoglycemia with seizures or for diabetic ketoacidosis. A transplant psychologist documents that she understands the surgical risks and is able to manage lifelong immunosuppression, and the transplant team finds her otherwise a suitable candidate. Her kidney function is normal (eGFR 92) and she has never had a kidney transplant.
cases.note: Pancreas alone: autoantibody results pending and no fasting C-peptide, so type 1 diabetes is not yet shown.

cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with end-stage ischemic cardiomyopathy supported by a durable LVAD for 2 years, now matched with a donor heart. The transplant will be performed at a hospital whose heart transplant program is approved by Medicare as meeting the institutional coverage criteria.
cases.note: Transplant at a Medicare-approved facility. Age 67 and prior LVAD are not facility criteria.

cases.vignette: 59-year-old woman with restrictive cardiomyopathy listed for heart transplant. The transplant will be performed at one of two hospitals under common control of a university health system that function as a single heart transplant facility: the same transplant surgeons, cardiologists, and pathologists practice at both, they use the same organ procurement organization and tissue-typing services, and they have operated the program for 12 years. CMS has approved this two-hospital facility as a Medicare heart transplant facility.
cases.note: Two-hospital university facility that CMS approved as a heart transplant facility (not a consortium).

cases.vignette: 15-year-old Medicare beneficiary (entitled through end-stage renal disease) with dilated cardiomyopathy awaiting heart transplant at a pediatric hospital that performs pediatric heart transplants. The pediatric hospital submitted an application, which CMS approved, documenting that its program is operated jointly with an adult center that CMS has found meets the institutional coverage criteria, that the unified program shares the same transplant surgeons and quality assurance program, and that it provides the specialized facilities, services, and personnel pediatric heart transplant patients require.
cases.note: Pediatric hospital whose application CMS approved.
